title.rendered: How to Auto Scroll on Instagram Reels

content.rendered:
Gone are the days when you had to scroll through Reels manually. Instagram has finally introduced Auto-Scroll for Reels, a feature that automatically advances to the next Reel once the current one finishes playing. This new addition makes watching Reels more immersive, especially during long viewing sessions where constant swiping can feel disruptive.

Keep reading to learn how to enable Auto-Scroll for Reels on Instagram.

Table of Contents
  • What Is Auto-Scroll on Instagram Reels?
  • How to Enable Auto-Scroll for Instagram Reels
  • Does Auto-Scroll Work on Instagram Web?
  • How to Use Auto-Scroll for Reels on a Mac
  • What to Do If Auto-Scroll Isn't Showing on Instagram
  • Less Control, More Watching…

What Is Auto-Scroll on Instagram Reels?

Auto-Scroll is a new playback setting in the Instagram mobile app that lets Reels play automatically, one after another. Instead of swiping up, the next Reel loads and starts playing on its own.

How to Enable Auto-Scroll for Instagram Reels

  1. Open the Instagram app and head to your Reels feed.
  2. Here, tap the three-dot button on the currently playing Reel.
  3. Next, toggle on Auto-Scroll.

Once enabled, Reels will continue playing automatically without requiring a swipe up.

Does Auto-Scroll Work on Instagram Web?

At the moment, Auto-Scroll for Reels is primarily designed for the Instagram mobile app and is still rolling out gradually. This means the feature is not yet available to all users, even on iPhone and Android. Availability depends on factors such as account type, region, and Instagram’s server-side rollouts.

As a result, users watching Reels on Instagram Web still need to manually move between videos.

How to Use Auto-Scroll for Reels on a Mac

While there is no official word on when Instagram will roll out Auto-Scroll for Reels on Instagram Web, Mac users are not entirely left out. Even without a native toggle on the desktop site, you can still experience Instagram’s official Auto-Scroll feature on a Mac by using the iPhone Mirroring app.

Since Auto-Scroll is supported in the Instagram mobile app, enabling it on your iPhone automatically carries over when the app is mirrored to macOS.

To use Auto-Scroll for Instagram Reels on a Mac:

  1. Enable Auto-Scroll in the Instagram app on your iPhone.
  2. Now, open the iPhone Mirroring app on your Mac and launch Instagram from the mirrored iPhone interface.
  3. Once a Reel starts playing, videos will advance automatically, just as they do on your phone.

What to Do If Auto-Scroll Isn’t Showing on Instagram

If you don’t see the Auto-Scroll option for Reels, there is likely nothing wrong with your account or device.

  • Update the Instagram app to the latest version from the App Store or Play Store.
  • Confirm you are watching Reels in full screen from the Reels tab.
  • Log out of your Instagram account and sign back in to refresh account-level features.
  • Check another account on the same device to confirm rollout differences.
  • Remember that Auto-Scroll is a gradual server-side rollout and may not be enabled for all users yet.

Less Control, More Watching…

While Auto-Scroll may seem like a small quality-of-life update, it carries broader implications for how people consume Reels. By removing the need to swipe manually, Instagram reduces the pauses that previously gave users a sense of control. The result is a more passive viewing experience that makes it easier to lose track of time and end up watching far more Reels than originally intended.

Have you noticed Auto Scroll in your Instagram app yet, or do you prefer manual control while watching Reels? Share your thoughts in the comments.

  • Instagram Map Lets You See Where Friends Are and What’s Happening Nearby
  • Link Reels on Instagram: Everything You Need to Know

title.rendered: Best Apple Pencil Grips You Can Buy Right Now

content.rendered:
If your Apple Pencil tends to slip from your hold, digs into your finger grooves, or strains your wrist during long writing or drawing sessions, a well-designed grip can completely change how it feels. In this guide, I share the best Apple Pencil grips available right now, along with a practical buying guide and top picks for writing, artists, kids, and everyday use.

Whether you are a student taking fast notes, a professional annotating documents, a digital artist sketching for hours, or someone dealing with hand fatigue, the right Apple Pencil grip can make a noticeable difference.

Table of Contents
  • What Is an Apple Pencil Grip and Why It Matters
  • Types of Apple Pencil Grips Explained
  • How to Choose the Best Apple Pencil Grip
    • Apple Pencil Generation Compatibility
    • Comfort vs Precision Tradeoffs
    • Grip Thickness and Hand Size
    • Attachment Style and Ease of Removal
    • Case and Charging Compatibility
  • Best Apple Pencil Grips by Use Case
    • 1. UPPERCASE NimbleGrip: Everyday Writing & Note-Taking
    • 2. Paperlike Pencil Grips: For Artists & Designers
    • 3. elago Apple Pencil Case: Slim & Protective
    • 4. ProElife Ergonomics Grip Holder: Budget Multi-Pack
    • 5. Ringke Silicone Drafting Grip: Non-Slip Textured Grip
    • 6. AFOOYO 5-Pack Pencil Grips: Multi-purpose Usage
  • How to Use and Maintain Apple Pencil Grips
    • Installing and Adjusting Your Grip
    • Cleaning and Caring for Silicone Grips
    • Troubleshooting Charging or Magnetic Issues
  • Final Thoughts

What Is an Apple Pencil Grip and Why It Matters

An Apple Pencil grip is a soft sleeve or case that slides over the Pencil to add comfort, traction, and shape. Most modern grips are designed so you can still use magnetic charging and touch-based gestures without removing them.

Key Benefits:

  • Ergonomics & comfort: Soft materials and curved shapes spread pressure, reducing finger soreness and wrist strain.
  • Better control: Textured surfaces and thicker barrels make fine strokes and long lines steadier.
  • Protection: Grips protect the Pencil from scratches, minor bumps, and accidental drops.
  • Custom feel: You can change the thickness, shape, or texture without replacing the Pencil.

Therefore, as a student taking rapid notes, a professional annotating documents, a digital artist sketching for hours, teaching a kid how to hold a stylus, or struggling with hand movements, having the right grip on an Apple Pencil can be a game-changer.

Types of Apple Pencil Grips Explained

  • Round silicone sleeves: Simple, inexpensive, and add cushion. Good for everyday writing.
  • Ergonomic tri- or hex shapes: Give a defined resting place for fingers (reduces twisting).
  • Thick “pencil-like” grips: Mimic regular pencil thickness for long comfort. Writers favor this one.
  • Hybrid grips/cases with built-in clips or stands: Offer protection and storage plus grip.
  • Multi-pack universal sleeves: Cheap options to test different shapes and sizes.

How to Choose the Best Apple Pencil Grip

Before hitting add to cart, keep the following in mind to find the right one:

Apple Pencil Generation Compatibility

Check whether the grip is designed for Apple Pencil 1st gen, 2nd gen, USB-C Pencil, or the Apple Pencil Pro. Some grips are “universal” while others explicitly fit only the 2nd gen and Pencil Pro, as they have a flat side for magnetic charging.

Comfort vs Precision Tradeoffs

Thicker or softer grips are more comfortable but can slightly change how the Pencil balances and how you see the tip while drawing. Artists requiring complete control may find thinner precision grips more useful, while note-takers may require softer and thicker grips.

Grip Thickness and Hand Size

Small hands or children may prefer grips to be finer, while writing adults tend to prefer thicker grips to ease muscle strain in the hands.

Attachment Style and Ease of Removal

Look for grips that slip on easily and come off without leaving residue. If you charge magnetically or rely on double-tap, choose a grip that can be partially removed or has a cutout for the tap area.

Case and Charging Compatibility

If you magnetically charge or mount (Apple Pencil 2/USB-C/Pro), confirm the grip allows the functionality. Also, go for a thin grip if you store the Pencil in your iPad case.

Best Apple Pencil Grips by Use Case

Below are the top picks for everyday writing, artists, and kids. Each one includes the use case and what to expect.

1. UPPERCASE NimbleGrip: Everyday Writing & Note-Taking

UPPERCASE NimbleGrip ergonomic finger grip is made of soft, premium silicone to reduce hand fatigue. It has a dual-sided exterior (round and hex) so you can choose the feel and orientation. Moreover, the interior ribbed design fits your Pencil like a glove.

The grip can be used with all Apple Pencil models, but you need to remove it for wireless charging. For storage, you can buy UPPERCASE NimbleStand. This Pencil holder is useful to keep your stylus handy and avoid losing it.

Why pick it: simple, comfortable, and made for long sessions. Good for students and office use.

2. Paperlike Pencil Grips: For Artists & Designers

Designed for precision and feel for creatives, Paperlike Pencil grips aim to maintain a tactile, natural hold with a slender ergonomic shape. Its broad cushioning helps in precise control without hand fatigue.

Paperlike has used high-quality, recyclable silicone for durability and comfort. The best part is that the grip works with all the models and supports every Apple Pencil feature, including Double Tap Gesture, Barrel Roll, Squeeze, and even wireless charging.

Why pick it: artists who sketch for long hours and want both precision and comfort.

3. elago Apple Pencil Case: Slim & Protective

elago’s grip sleeve is designed with Apple Pencil 2/Pro’s magnetic charging and double-tap capabilities in mind. It covers the entire Pencil to protect it from scratches, bumps, and drops. You will also get a protection cap to safeguard the Pencil tail.

I like its old-school look with ergonomic hexagon design. The soft silicone ensures a strong grip and a snug fit. Its unique design ensures magnetic attachment and charging. Overall, you should buy this Apple Pencil case if you want protection while enjoying full Pencil features.

Why pick it: people who frequently magnetically charge and want a thin protective sleeve.

4. ProElife Ergonomics Grip Holder: Budget Multi-Pack

If you are looking for a budget-friendly finger grip for your Apple Pencil 2/Pro/USB-C, go for this one. Made of high-quality silicon with special molding, the sleeve is stretchy and only 0.5mm thick. You can quickly install it and attach it or wirelessly charge your Pencil.

The concave design ensures firm holding and a soft feel. Moreover, you get two grips in an affordable bundle, providing great value.

Why pick it: low cost, multiple grips, good for students or teams.

5. Ringke Silicone Drafting Grip: Non-Slip Textured Grip

A more structured soft silicone cover with threaded/textured engravings for non-slip cushioned hold and an ergonomic shape. Ringke’s optimized thickness design aims to preserve Double Tap and charging features while improving grip.

It’s universally compatible with all Apple Pencil models. If you have sweaty hands, this grip prevents your Pencil from slipping off. However, as the cover goes till the Pencil tip, you need to remove the grip before tip replacement.

Why pick it: people who want a grippy, textured sleeve that stays put during sketching or note-taking.

6. AFOOYO 5-Pack Pencil Grips: Multi-purpose Usage

Multi-packs in bright colors, different designs, and widths. You can switch between the grips as needed. The hexagonal design is anti-rolling and supports wireless charging.

If you use an iPad case with a pencil holder, ensure it has an anti-slip design. All the grips feature soft silicone for a smooth surface. However, note that you can use them with Apple Pencil 1st gen.

Why pick it: beginners, kids, and anyone who wants a palette of inexpensive grips to try.

How to Use and Maintain Apple Pencil Grips

Now that you have chosen your grip holder, let’s see how to utilize it.

Installing and Adjusting Your Grip

  1. Pencil cleaning: Use a dry cloth to gently rub away oils or dust.
  2. Slide smoothly: Gently stretch the silicone and slide it from the tip to the eraser end of the pencil.
  3. Position on the device: Bulbous/thick part should be positioned in a place where the fingers rest during writing. When drawing, this should be higher so that the wrist can move.
  4. Test features: If you use double-tap or magnetic charging, leave the recommended gap or follow the brand’s instructions so features still work.

Cleaning and Caring for Silicone Grips

With daily usage, your Pencil grip can become greasy and attract lint and dust. So, you must clean it regularly.

Remove the grip from your pencil first for safety. Use mild dish soap and warm water to clean the silicone grip, then rinse gently. Then use a soft, lint-free cloth to absorb the water and let it air-dry.

Avoid acetone or harsh cleaners as they can degrade silicone. Ensure your grip is completely dry before putting it on. Also, store the Pencil in a case or sleeve when not in use.

Troubleshooting Charging or Magnetic Issues

You can also replace the grip if it becomes torn or permanently discolored to keep your pencil looking sharp.

Final Thoughts

Apple Pencil grips are one of the cheapest and most effective ways to improve comfort and control. Decide based on:

  • Your Pencil model (1st gen vs 2nd gen vs USB-C/Pro),
  • Your primary use (notes vs art vs kids),
  • Whether you need magnetic charging or double-tap access.

If you write a lot, softer and thicker grips like UPPERCASE or ProElife are excellent. Artists may prefer Paperlike or Ringke for precision and texture. For kids or classrooms, multi-packs like AFOOYO offer flexibility and value.

For such a small investment, a good grip can prevent fatigue, improve accuracy, and make your Apple Pencil feel brand new again. Which one caught your eye? Let me know in the comments.

FAQs

Are Apple Pencil grips worth it?

Yes. For frequent users, the comfort and reduced hand strain alone justify the small cost.

Do grips affect sensitivity or accuracy?

No. The Pencil tip interacts with the screen the same way. Very thick grips may slightly change balance, but pressure sensitivity remains unchanged.

Will grips interfere with magnetic charging?

Some do. Many modern grips are designed to support charging, either fully or with easy removal. Always check product compatibility.

Do grips work with Pencil holders and cases?

Most do, but thick grips may not fit tight Pencil slots. Slim grips are safer if you use a holder or case.

Editorial Note: When you purchase through our links, we earn a small commission. However, this does not affect our opinions or evaluations. Learn more about our Editorial Process and Disclaimer.

mainEntity.name: Can I restore the original image after removing the background?

acceptedAnswer.text: iPhone background removal tools do not overwrite the original photo. Therefore, your original image remains unchanged, and background-removed versions are created as separate copies.

mainEntity.name: Is there a cost involved with third-party apps?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many third-party apps offer free background removal with basic features. However, advanced options such as high-resolution exports, batch processing, or refined edge controls often require a subscription or one-time purchase.

mainEntity.name: Does removing the background affect image quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: Background removal does not reduce image quality by itself, but the final result depends on the tool used. Built-in tools may struggle with fine details, while professional apps usually preserve sharper edges and better transparency.

@graph.name: UPPERCASE NimbleGrip
@graph.description: UPPERCASE NimbleGrip ergonomic finger grip is made of soft, premium silicone to reduce hand fatigue. It has a dual-sided exterior (round and hex) so you can choose the feel and orientation. The grip can be used with all Apple Pencil models, but you need to remove it for wireless charging.

@graph.name: UPPERCASE NimbleStand
@graph.description: NimbleStand safely holds your Apple Pencil above any mess while keeping it within reach when inspiration hits. A weighted aluminum insert keeps NimbleStand secure on your desk and allows the Apple Pencil to sit vertically or horizontally when resting in between tasks. Made with premium silicone, the Apple Pencil accessory is perfect for digital creatives looking to add to their setup with a stand that complements the iPad and Apple Pencil.

@graph.name: Paperlike Pencil Grips for Apple Pencil
@graph.description: Designed for precision and feel for creatives, Paperlike Pencil grips aim to maintain a tactile, natural hold with a slender ergonomic shape. Its broad cushioning helps in precise control without hand fatigue. Paperlike has used high-quality, recyclable silicone for durability and comfort. The best part is that the grip works with all the models and supports every Apple Pencil feature, including Double Tap Gesture, Barrel Roll, Squeeze, and even wireless charging.

@graph.name: elago Apple Pencil Case
@graph.description: elago’s grip sleeve is designed with Apple Pencil 2/Pro’s magnetic charging and double-tap capabilities in mind. It covers the entire Pencil to protect it from scratches, bumps, and drops. You will also get a protection cap to safeguard the Pencil tail.

@graph.name: ProElife Ergonomics Grip Holder
@graph.description: If you are looking for a budget-friendly finger grip for your Apple Pencil 2/Pro/USB-C, go for this one. Made of high-quality silicon with special molding, the sleeve is stretchy and only 0.5mm thick. You can quickly install it and attach it or wirelessly charge your Pencil.

@graph.name: Ringke Silicone Drafting Grip
@graph.description: A more structured soft silicone cover with threaded/textured engravings for non-slip cushioned hold and an ergonomic shape. Ringke’s optimized thickness design aims to preserve Double Tap and charging features while improving grip. It’s universally compatible with all Apple Pencil models.

@graph.name: AFOOYO 5-Pack Pencil Grips
@graph.description: Multi-packs in bright colors, different designs, and widths. You can switch between the grips as needed. The hexagonal design is anti-rolling and supports wireless charging. If you use an iPad case with a pencil holder, ensure it has an anti-slip design. All the grips feature soft silicone for a smooth surface.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
"The founder of iGeeksBlog, Dhvanesh, is an Apple aficionado, who cannot stand even a slight innuendo about Apple products. He dons the cap of editor-in-chief to make sure that articles match the quality standard before they are published."

About Dhvanesh

Ever since teenage years, gadgets and technology have held a special place in Dhvanesh's heart. This fascination with gadgets and their inner workings fueled a lifelong passion for exploration and troubleshooting. Disassembled electronic items scattered around the house became a familiar sight during his younger years, a testament to this insatiable curiosity.

From SEO Expert to Apple Evangelist

After completing his IT engineering diploma, Dhvanesh's professional journey began with a 4.5-year stint as an SEO executive, honing valuable digital marketing skills. However, the desire to share tech knowledge and connect with a like-minded community proved stronger. In 2012, Dhvanesh embarked on a new adventure, founding iGeeksBlog. This blog became a haven for Apple enthusiasts and tech aficionados seeking insightful and in-depth information about everything Apple.

A Decade of iGeeksBlog: Leading the Apple Charge

In the past 12 years, Dhvanesh has donned multiple hats at iGeeksBlog. As the founder, he has steered the blog’s vision, ensuring it remains a trusted resource for Apple users worldwide. Additionally, he has been serving as the CEO of iGeeks Media Private Limited for the past 4 years, overseeing the company's growth and development.

Beyond Writing: A Multifaceted Approach

Dhvanesh isn't just a prolific writer, having penned hundreds of articles for iGeeksBlog. He has also served as the blog’s Editor-in-Chief and Content Strategist, ensuring a consistent flow of high-quality content that caters to the diverse needs of the Apple user base. The passion for exploration extends beyond the written word. He has created numerous YouTube videos for iGeeksBlog, providing visual demonstrations and engaging directly with the audience.

Staying Connected with the Apple Ecosystem

Dhvanesh's dedication to the Apple community goes a step further. Currently, he also manages the iGeeksBlog+ weekly newsletter, delivering curated Apple news, gadgets, apps, tips and tricks straight to subscribers' inboxes. This unwavering commitment to Apple technology and a genuine desire to empower fellow users make him a valuable asset to the iGeeksBlog team.

title.rendered: How to Organize Photos on Mac Like a Pro

content.rendered:
If your Photos library feels chaotic, it is usually the same mix every time: duplicates wasting storage, screenshots and downloads blending into real memories, and photos scattered across devices and random folders. And if you are a photographer or content creator, it gets 10 times worse with the management. In this guide, I will show you how you can optimize your photos and maybe even other folders on your Mac. Let’s begin. 

Table of Contents
  • How Photos Are Stored on Mac
  • Photos App vs Finder: Which Should You Use
  • Prepare Before You Start Organizing
  • Use the Photos App to Organize Photos on Mac
    • 1. Use Years, Months, and Days to Navigate First
    • 2. Create Albums and Folders Without Overdoing It
    • 3. Use a Clear Album Naming Strategy
    • 4. Use Search, People, and Places Instead of More Albums
    • 5. Use Smart Albums to Handle Repeat Clutter
    • 6. Use Favorites and Keywords Sparingly
    • 7. Clean Up Regularly in Small Passes
    • 8. Remove Duplicates and Similar Photos Carefully
    • 9. Tidy Screenshots and Random Images
    • 10. Hide Photos from Library
    • 11. Curate Burst Photos and Live Photos
  • Organize Photos Using Finder (Advanced Users)
    • 1. Know When Finder-Based Organization Makes Sense
    • 2. Create a Clear Finder Folder Hierarchy
    • 3. Export Photos From Photos Before Using Finder
    • 4. Rename Photo Files Only When It Matters
    • 5. Manage Storage With External Drives and iCloud
  • Optimize Mac Storage With iCloud Photos
    • 1. Move or Create a Photos Library on an External Drive
    • 2. Daily and Monthly Habits to Stay Organized
    • 3. Quick Weekly Photo Organization Routine
    • 4. Monthly Deep Clean and Backup
  • Conclusion

How Photos Are Stored on Mac

On a Mac, photos usually live in two places, and each one works differently.

Photos imported into the Photos app are stored inside a single Photos Library file in the Pictures folder. You do not see or manage individual image files in Finder. The Photos app controls storage, edits, and organization for you.

If iCloud Photos is turned on, this same library is shared across your devices. Edits and deletions sync automatically, and macOS may keep smaller versions on your Mac while storing full originals in iCloud.

Photos that are not in the Photos app are just normal files. Anything in Downloads, Desktop, project folders, or external drives is handled by Finder. You can move, rename, and back up these files freely, and they do not sync unless you set that up yourself.

Before organizing, you need to know which photos are managed by Photos and which ones are regular files. Everything you do next depends on that.

Photos App vs Finder: Which Should You Use

For most users, the Photos app should be the main method. It is built to handle huge libraries because it relies on search and metadata, not manual folder browsing.

Photos app is best when you want to search by date, place, person, object, or event. It also gives you People and Places grouping, Smart Albums, and iCloud syncing.

Finder based organization makes sense when you need strict file control. For example, you are keeping a separate archive on an external drive, or you are managing client and project folders where filenames and folder paths matter.

The safest approach is simple: use Photos for your main library, and use Finder only for archives or advanced workflows. Do not try to replace Photos search with endless Finder folders.

Prepare Before You Start Organizing

Before you start organizing, take a few minutes to set things up so you do not create more mess later.

  • Make sure macOS and the Photos app are updated.
  • If you use iCloud Photos, check that the same Apple Account is signed in on all devices.
  • Find your Photos Library in the Pictures folder so you know which file matters.
  • Delete obvious blur shots, accidental screenshots, and junk you do not need.
  • Fix wrong dates and locations for scanned or old imported photos.
  • Back up your photo library using Time Machine, or quit Photos and copy the Photos Library to an external drive.
  • Import photos from phones, cameras, old drives, and folders like Downloads and Desktop into one main Photos library. Start with the most recent year if you have a lot.

Once this is done, organizing is faster and much safer.

Use the Photos App to Organize Photos on Mac

The Photos app is designed to manage large libraries without you manually moving files around. The platform already offers the needed features and options. Here’s how you can use them to organize and manage your photos on Apple Photos. 

1. Use Years, Months, and Days to Navigate First

Photos automatically organizes your entire library by time, and this should always be your starting point.

Use Years to jump to a broad time period, Months to spot trips or events, and Days when you remember roughly when something happened. This is often faster than browsing albums.

If scanned photos or old imports appear in the wrong year, fix the date so time-based browsing works correctly.

To fix dates:

  1. Right-click on the image
  2. Select Get info.
  3. Click on the date and time.
  4. Correct the year or date and click Adjust.

Once dates are correct, browsing works consistently everywhere in Photos.

2. Create Albums and Folders Without Overdoing It

Albums help group photos you actually revisit. They are collections, not storage locations, so adding a photo to an album does not move it or create duplicates. Folders are only used to organize albums in the sidebar.

A structure that works long-term:

  • Year folders for personal photos
  • Event albums only for meaningful trips or moments
  • One small “Useful” folder for receipts, documents, and reference images

You can create albums and folders that make more sense to your needs.

To create an album: You can do that directly by clicking the plus icon beside Albums option in sidebar. Alternatively, you can

  1. Select all the photos that you want to place in an Album.
  2. Click File → New Album
  3. Name the album

Albums can be renamed, reordered, or moved into folders at any time without affecting the photos themselves. You can also add and remove photos to and from the album anytime.

3. Use a Clear Album Naming Strategy

Album names should sort themselves so you do not need manual ordering.

Use date-first naming:

  • YYYY-MM Event name

This keeps albums in order automatically. For old scanned photos, use the closest known year or group by decade so they do not mix with recent photos.

4. Use Search, People, and Places Instead of More Albums

Search is often more powerful than albums.

You can search by people, pets, places, objects, scenes, or even text inside images. This removes the need to manually organize everything.

In People, name important faces once, and Photos groups them automatically. If the same person appears twice, merge them sothe results stay clean.

Places uses location data and helps when you remember where something happened, but not the date.

This is why you do not need an album for every topic.

5. Use Smart Albums to Handle Repeat Clutter

Smart Albums update automatically based on rules, which makes them ideal for things that keep piling up.

To create one:

  1. Click File → New Smart Album
  2. Name the album
  3. Set conditions like media type, date range, favorites, or keywords
  4. Click OK

Smart Albums that actually help:

  • Screenshots
  • Videos
  • Last 30 Days
  • Favorites this year

These Smart Albums also make cleanup easier later because clutter gathers itself.

6. Use Favorites and Keywords Sparingly

Favorites are the fastest way to surface photos you care about. Click the heart and move on.

Keywords are simple labels added from the Info panel.

To add keywords:

  1. Open a photo.
  2. Press ⌘ (command) + I.
  3. Add keywords like receipts, documents, travel, work, or family.

Keep keywords small and practical. This improves search and Smart Albums without adding maintenance work.

7. Clean Up Regularly in Small Passes

Organizing without deleting junk never feels finished.

Start with obvious blur shots, accidental screenshots, and images you clearly do not need. Do cleanup in short sessions so it does not feel overwhelming.

Deleted photos go to Recently Deleted, giving you a safety window before permanent removal.

8. Remove Duplicates and Similar Photos Carefully

On newer macOS versions, Photos includes a Duplicates section where exact copies can be reviewed and merged.

Review before merging. Similar-looking photos are not always true duplicates.

If your Mac does not show a Duplicates section, review manually or use a trusted tool, but always preview before deleting.

9. Tidy Screenshots and Random Images

Screenshots often create the most noise in a library.

Use Media Types or the Smart Albums you created earlier to gather screenshots automatically. Keep what matters and delete the rest. If some screenshots are important, move them into a dedicated album like Receipts or Reference. This keeps personal photos easy to browse.

10. Hide Photos from Library

If you prefer to keep some photos hidden from others or you just wanna keep clutter away from daily use, you can hide the photos completely. You can unhide them anytime if you want, and you can even select multiple and hide all of them at once.

11. Curate Burst Photos and Live Photos

Burst photos are created when you hold the shutter button and capture many frames in a second.

To clean them:

  1. Open the burst
  2. Select the best frame
  3. Delete the rest

Live Photos include a few seconds of motion and sound. Keep them when movement adds value. If not, converting them to still photos helps reduce clutter.

Organize Photos Using Finder (Advanced Users)

Finder-based organization is useful when you need real files in real folders. This applies to long-term archives, photography projects, or client work where folder paths, filenames, and exports matter. It is not meant to replace the Photos app for everyday memories.

The biggest risk here is mixing systems. The Photos library and Finder archives must stay separate. You should never move or rename files inside the Photos Library package, and you should be clear about which photos live in Photos and which live in Finder.

1. Know When Finder-Based Organization Makes Sense

Use Finder when:

  • You need exact file paths and filenames
  • You work with clients or external tools
  • You want a long-term archive independent of Photos

Do not use Finder to manage photos that already live inside the Photos app unless you export them first. Treat Photos Library.photoslibrary as untouchable.

If iCloud Photos is enabled, remember that deleting a photo in Photos removes it across devices. This is another reason to keep Finder archives clearly separate.

2. Create a Clear Finder Folder Hierarchy

Start with one top-level folder, then organize by year, then by event or shoot. Date-first naming keeps everything sorted automatically.

A simple structure that scales:

  • Photos Archive
    • 2024 Images
      • 24-01-24 Blackpool
    • 2025 Images
      • 25-06-10 Wedding – Anya

Keep names predictable. This makes folders sortable, searchable, and easy to restore later.

Never edit anything inside Photos Library.photoslibrary. If you want photos in Finder, either export them from Photos or copy originals directly from your camera into this archive.

3. Export Photos From Photos Before Using Finder

If photos already live in the Photos app, export them properly instead of dragging files around.

To export safely:

  1. Open Photos and select the images
  2. Click File → Export → Export Unmodified Originals
  3. Choose your Finder archive folder

This keeps Photos intact and gives you clean files to work with in Finder.

4. Rename Photo Files Only When It Matters

Renaming is useful for client delivery, shared folders, or long-term archives you might access outside Photos.

Finder makes batch renaming easy:

  1. Select multiple files
  2. Right-click and choose Rename
  3. Use Add Text, Replace Text, or Format

Inside the Photos app, filenames matter much less. Photos relies on dates, metadata, People, Places, keywords, and search. Do not waste time renaming files that stay inside Photos.

5. Manage Storage With External Drives and iCloud

Finder-based archives are often used when storage is tight.

A clean setup is to keep your current year photos inside Photos and move older years to a Finder archive on an external drive. This keeps your daily library fast while preserving everything.

If you use iCloud Photos, enabling Optimize Mac Storage allows macOS to keep smaller local versions while full originals stay in iCloud. This does not change how your photos are organized, only how they are stored.

The key is consistency. Photos manages your active library. Finder manages your archives. Mixing the two without a plan is how photos get lost.

Optimize Mac Storage With iCloud Photos

Optimize Mac Storage keeps smaller versions on your Mac and pulls originals when needed. Your albums, People, Places, and search still work the same. It is a storage strategy, not an organization change.

1. Move or Create a Photos Library on an External Drive

Move a library safely like this:

  1. Quit Photos.
  2. Copy Photos Library.photoslibrary to the external drive.
  3. Hold Option while opening Photos.
  4. Choose the library on the external drive.

Photos can open only one library at a time. Multiple libraries make sense only if you truly want separation, like a personal library and a work archive.

2. Daily and Monthly Habits to Stay Organized

The easiest way to stay organized is to do tiny actions regularly, instead of massive cleanups once a year. Favorite your best shots when you notice them. Drop big events into the right album. Delete obvious junk quickly so it does not pile up.

3. Quick Weekly Photo Organization Routine

Spend 10 to 15 minutes once a week:

  1. Import new photos.
  2. Delete obvious junk.
  3. Favorite the best shots.
  4. Add major events to an album.
  5. Confirm iCloud finished syncing if you use it.

4. Monthly Deep Clean and Backup

Once a month: Review duplicates, clean screenshots and downloads, fix People names, and confirm your backups are current. A recurring reminder helps because this is easy to forget.

Conclusion

Start with a backup, consolidate into one main library, then organize inside Photos using time views, a small album and folder structure, People, Places, and a few Smart Albums.

You do not need to finish everything at once. Start with the most recent year first. That is where you search the most, and it gives you quick wins.

FAQs

What is the best way to organize photos on Mac for most users?

Use the Photos app as your main library. Keep a small set of albums for trips and important events, use Favorites, and rely on Search, People, and Places.

Should I organize photos on Mac in Photos app or in Finder folders?

Photos for personal libraries and iCloud syncing. Finder folders only for archives or workflows where you need real files.

Will organizing photos on my Mac affect photos on my iPhone?

Yes, if iCloud Photos is enabled. Albums, edits, favorites, and deletions sync across devices signed into the same Apple Account

How long does it take to organize a large photo library on Mac?

It depends on size and mess, but the fastest approach is to organize the recent months first, then work backward in short weekly sessions.

title.rendered: Apple’s New AI Tool Generates 3D Scenes from a Single Image

content.rendered:
Apple has unveiled an AI model called SHARP, designed to transform a solitary photograph into a detailed 3D scene in less than a second. Unlike traditional methods necessitating multiple images and lengthy processing, SHARP delivers photorealistic results with just one image as input, producing rapid outcomes in real time.

Reconstructing 3D Scenes with Just One Photo

SHARP’s foundation is a deep learning system that converts a single picture into a 3D Gaussian representation. This innovative method involves blending millions of minuscule colored light blobs within 3D space to recreate the scene.

Conventional 3D synthesis models require 30 to 100 photos taken from various angles to build a complete scene, whereas SHARP circumvents this need entirely. The model processes merely one pass through a neural network, outputting a scene that can be examined from nearby perspectives. It achieves this while preserving high resolution and precise spatial details.

How SHARP Maintains Real-World Scale

A standout feature of SHARP is its metric accuracy, ensuring that 3D reconstructions maintain true-to-life scale, with realistic and consistent camera movements and depth. This capability arises from SHARP’s training with extensive datasets of both real and synthetic images, enabling the model to learn generalized depth and structural geometry. This training allows it to accurately estimate the position and appearance of millions of 3D points, even in scenes it’s encountering for the first time.

Faster and More Accurate Than Previous Methods

SHARP’s advantages extend beyond mere speed; it also enhances quality. When put head to head with Gen3C, a robust earlier model, SHARP demonstrates:

  • 25–34% reduction in LPIPS (perceptual similarity error)
  • 21–43% reduction in DISTS (structural similarity error)
  • A remarkable 1000 times increase in rendering speed

This model can provide real-time renderings on standard GPUs, making real-time applications feasible for developers, designers, and researchers.

One Limitation: Works Best for Nearby Views

Although SHARP excels in rendering realistic nearby perspectives, it does have its constraints. It’s not designed to invent unseen parts of the scene beyond the initial image’s scope. This limitation is part of the tradeoff for higher speed and stability; SHARP refrains from creating speculative geometry, focusing instead on delivering precise renderings within a close viewing range of the original photo.

SHARP is Available for Public Use

Apple has made SHARP accessible via GitHub, encouraging developers to experiment firsthand. Early adopters have already begun posting demos and experiments, showcasing rotated views and animations derived from a single static image.

This technology could potentially revolutionize areas such as augmented reality, virtual staging, 3D photography, and content creation, eliminating the need for elaborate multi-camera setups or prolonged training durations.

title.rendered: How to Share Location in Google Maps on iPhone

content.rendered:
Coordinating plans over text is often messier than it needs to be. In situations like meeting someone in a crowded place, traveling late at night, or keeping family informed during a long commute, static location sharing simply is not enough. This is where live location sharing becomes essential. Instead of constant updates and follow-up messages, Google Maps lets you share your real-time location from your iPhone so others can see exactly where you are and how fast you are moving.

This post details how to share your location in Google Maps on an iPhone, manage sharing duration, and stop location sharing instantly.

Table of Contents
  • Requirements Before You Share Your Location
  • How to Share your Real-Time Location in Google Maps on iPhone
  • How to Share Your Estimated Time of Arrival in Google Maps on iPhone
  • How Accurate Is Google Maps Location Sharing on iPhone
  • Common Issues and Fixes
  • Let's get going!

Requirements Before You Share Your Location

  • The sender and recipient must have a Google account.
  • Turn on Location Services on your iPhone.
  • Permit Google Maps to access your location. Go to Settings → Apps → Google Maps → Location → Select Always.
  • Don’t live in a country or region where Google’s location-sharing service is unavailable.

Besides, sharing location using Google Maps can reveal your personal information. After you share your live location with someone, they can see the following:

  • Your name and photo.
  • Your device’s recent location.
  • Your device’s battery level and charging status.
  • Your arrival and departure time if Location Sharing notification is enabled.

Moreover, the recipient can view other information based on your location-sharing method.

Now that you know the prerequisites to share your current location on Google Maps let’s see how!

How to Share your Real-Time Location in Google Maps on iPhone

  1. Launch Google Maps.
  2. Tap your profile → Select Location Sharing.
  3. Tap Share Location.
  4. Tap For 1 hour → Use the plus (+) and minus (–) icons to set the duration for sharing your location.
    Select Until you turn this off to disable location sharing manually.
  5. Select the user profile from the share sheet.
  6. To send the location-sharing link via other apps, tap More options.
  7. Hit the Share to generate a link for your location.
    Toggle on Don’t show this again if you prefer to share your location directly.
  8. Now, choose an app to send your live location link or copy the link.

    In any instance, if you wish to stop sharing your location in Google Maps, tap Sharing via the link and press Stop. This step will get you back to the standard interface.

How to Share Your Estimated Time of Arrival in Google Maps on iPhone

Apart from sharing your live location, Google Maps also enables you to share your estimated arrival time on Google Maps with others. Sounds fun, right? Follow the steps outlined below!

  1. Launch Google Maps → Tap the Direction icon.
  2. Choose starting point and destination applicable to you.
  3. Start your journey and swipe up the interface.
  4. Now press Share trip progress → Select the users with whom you wish to share your ETA.
  5. Tap More options → Copy to get your live ETA link.
  6. To stop your ETA from being shared, swipe up the shared interface → Tap Stop Sharing.

How Accurate Is Google Maps Location Sharing on iPhone

Google Maps uses a combination of GPS, Wi Fi, mobile networks, and motion sensors. With Precise Location enabled, accuracy is usually within a few meters. Accuracy may drop indoors, in low signal areas, or when battery saver mode is active.

Common Issues and Fixes

If location sharing does not work as expected, check the following:

  • Google Maps location permission is set to Always or While Using
  • Precise Location is turned on
  • Background app refresh is enabled
  • Low Power Mode is turned off
  • The internet connection is stable

Restarting the app or signing out and back into your Google account also resolves most issues.

Let’s get going!

Google’s location-sharing ability is nothing less than bliss. Whether you’re exploring a new area or checking in with a friend, it helps to stay connected and safe. So, try using this fantastic feature of Google Maps whenever you’re unfamiliar with your destination, and rest assured. If you face any issues, don’t hesitate to drop them below.

FAQs

Is it necessary to sign into Google Maps to share your location on your iPhone?

Yes, you are required to sign in to Google Maps if you seek to unlock its full potential.

Will sharing my location on Google Maps compromise my privacy?

It depends on how you set up your location-sharing settings. You can adjust your settings to share your location only with specific people or for a limited time. Also, you may turn off location sharing altogether if you don’t want to share your location at all.

Can I customize the message accompanying the location I share in Google Maps on iPhone?

Yes, you can customize the message accompanying the location you share on Google Maps to add a personal touch.

  • How to set up a shareable route that stays on track
  • Top Google Messages hidden features you should try

@graph.name: How to Share your Real-Time Location in Google Maps on iPhone
@graph.description: Learn how to easily share your live location with others using Google Maps on your iPhone. This guide walks you through each step with visuals for better understanding.

supply.name: An iPhone with Google Maps installed

step.name: Open Google Maps and go to Location Sharing
step.text: Launch Google Maps on your iPhone, tap your profile photo at the top right, then select Location Sharing from the menu.

itemListElement.text: Open the Google Maps app on your iPhone.
Tap your profile photo in the top-right corner.
Select Location Sharing from the list of options.

step.name: Set the location sharing duration
step.text: Tap Share Location and choose how long you'd like to share your live location. Use the plus and minus icons to adjust the time, or select 'Until you turn this off' to share indefinitely.

itemListElement.text: Tap Share Location to begin the process.
Choose the duration for location sharing using the plus and minus icons.
Select 'Until you turn this off' if you want to disable sharing manually later.

step.name: Choose who to share with
step.text: Pick a user profile from the list to share your location directly or tap More options to explore other sharing methods.

itemListElement.text: Select a user profile from the share sheet.
Tap More options to view other sharing methods.

step.name: Share your live location link
step.text: Hit the Share button to generate a shareable link. You can choose an app to send the link or simply copy it. Toggle on 'Don’t show this again' to streamline future shares.

itemListElement.text: Tap Share to generate your location link.
Select an app to send the link or tap Copy to copy it to your clipboard.
Toggle on 'Don’t show this again' if you want to skip the confirmation next time.

step.name: Stop sharing your location (optional)
step.text: If you wish to stop sharing your location at any point, tap on Sharing via the link and hit Stop. You’ll return to the regular Google Maps view.

itemListElement.text: Tap Sharing via the link.
Press Stop to end location sharing.

@graph.name: How to Share Your Estimated Time of Arrival in Google Maps on iPhone
@graph.description: Want to keep others updated on your ETA? Follow these easy steps to share your trip progress using Google Maps on your iPhone.

supply.name: An iPhone with Google Maps installed

step.name: Open Google Maps and set your route
step.text: Launch Google Maps, tap the Directions icon, and choose your starting point and destination.

itemListElement.text: Open the Google Maps app on your iPhone.
Tap the Directions icon.
Enter your starting point and destination.

step.name: Start navigation and swipe up
step.text: Begin your journey by tapping Start, then swipe up the interface to access more options.

itemListElement.text: Tap Start to begin navigation.
Swipe up from the bottom of the screen during your route.

step.name: Share your trip progress
step.text: Tap Share trip progress, then choose the users you want to notify or use More options to copy a shareable ETA link.

itemListElement.text: Tap Share trip progress.
Select the users you want to share your ETA with.
Tap More options and choose Copy to get a live ETA link.

step.name: Stop sharing your ETA (optional)
step.text: To stop sharing your ETA, swipe up the interface again and tap Stop Sharing. This will end the live update.

itemListElement.text: Swipe up the trip interface.
Tap Stop Sharing to end location updates.

keyPoints.title: Prerequisites for Sharing Location
keyPoints.explanation: Both sender and recipient need Google accounts, and location services must be enabled on the iPhone for live sharing to work.

keyPoints.title: Steps to Share Real-Time Location
keyPoints.explanation: Open Google Maps, access Location Sharing, select the duration, choose the recipient, and send the link to share your live location.

keyPoints.title: Sharing Estimated Arrival Time
keyPoints.explanation: Start a journey in Google Maps, share your trip progress, and select contacts to share your ETA, with options to stop sharing when needed.

keyPoints.title: Location Sharing Accuracy and Issues
keyPoints.explanation: Google Maps combines GPS, Wi-Fi, and mobile data for accuracy within a few meters, but indoor or low-signal areas may reduce precision, and restarting the app can fix common problems.

keyPoints.title: Privacy and Customization Tips
keyPoints.explanation: Location sharing can reveal personal info like your name, photo, and device status, but you can customize settings or turn off sharing to protect your privacy.

title.rendered: ChatGPT to Add Apple Music Integration for AI‑Generated Playlists

content.rendered:
ChatGPT is preparing to add Apple Music as a supported app, enabling users to create and play playlists directly via chat. The confirmation comes from OpenAI and points to a broader expansion of its in‑chat app ecosystem.

Apple Music Listed as an Upcoming ChatGPT App

In a Substack post published today, Fidji Simo, OpenAI’s CEO of Applications, said Apple Music is among the next apps planned for integration with ChatGPT. According to Simo, these apps will appear in a new directory that expands the current set of supported services.

Apple Music was mentioned alongside Adobe, Airtable, OpenTable, Replit, Salesforce, Clay, and Lovable. OpenAI also plans to allow other developers to submit their apps for review, suggesting a more open and scalable app ecosystem within ChatGPT.

The information was shared directly by Fidji Simo via Substack.

How Apple Music Is Expected to Work

OpenAI has not shared specific feature details, but Apple Music is expected to work similarly to Spotify’s existing ChatGPT integration. With Spotify, users can start a prompt by referencing the app, and ChatGPT activates it in the conversation to complete the request using the prompt’s context.

If Apple Music follows the same model, users could describe what they want to listen to in natural language and have ChatGPT generate an instantly playable playlist from Apple Music’s catalog. The focus is on reducing manual search and making music discovery more conversational.

A key advantage of this approach is its ability to handle vague or incomplete requests. Instead of recalling exact song titles or artists, users can describe moods, themes, or partial memories and let the language model translate that into relevant results.

What This Means for ChatGPT Apps

OpenAI first introduced apps in ChatGPT in October, partnering with Spotify, Canva, Booking.com, Coursera, Figma, Expedia, and Zillow. At the same time, it released a preview version of its Apps SDK for developers.

By announcing a larger app directory and naming high‑profile partners such as Apple Music, OpenAI is signaling that the Apps SDK is moving closer to broader availability beyond its preview phase.

Apple Music access through ChatGPT will still require an active subscription. Apple currently prices the service at $10.99 per month, with a one‑month free trial for new users.

OpenAI has not yet shared a rollout timeline, but more details about the Apple Music integration are expected in the coming days.

title.rendered: Apple in Talks to Assemble iPhone Chips in India for the First Time

content.rendered:
Apple is exploring the possibility of assembling and packaging iPhone chips in India, a move that would further deepen the company’s manufacturing footprint in the country. The information was first reported by The Economic Times, citing people familiar with the discussions.

Apple in early talks with CG Semi

According to The Economic Times, Apple is in preliminary conversations with CG Semi, an Indian semiconductor company, to handle assembly and packaging for future iPhone chips. These discussions are still at a very early stage, and no final decisions have been made.

CG Semi is currently building one of India’s first large-scale outsourced semiconductor assembly and test facilities, also known as an OSAT plant. The facility is located in Sanand and is expected to play a key role in India’s push to develop local semiconductor capabilities.

Sources told The Economic Times that it is not yet clear which iPhone chips could be handled at the Sanand facility. One person familiar with the matter said that display-related chips are the most likely candidates at this stage.

Why display chips are a likely starting point

Apple’s iPhone displays are supplied by companies such as Samsung Display, LG Display, and BOE. However, the display driver integrated circuits, which control how the display functions, are sourced from suppliers including Samsung, Novatek, Himax, and LX Semicon.

At present, these display chips are typically manufactured and packaged in facilities located in South Korea, Taiwan, or China. If Apple moves this part of the process to India, it would reduce reliance on existing packaging hubs and add another layer to its supply chain diversification strategy.

Part of Apple’s broader shift toward India

Any agreement with CG Semi would mark Apple’s first known attempt to assemble and package iPhone chips in India. Until now, India’s role in Apple’s supply chain has focused mainly on iPhone assembly.

Over the past few years, Apple has steadily increased its manufacturing presence in India as it looks to reduce dependence on China. Chip packaging would represent a more advanced step in this transition, moving beyond final device assembly into semiconductor-related operations.

India’s growing focus on chip manufacturing

The reported talks with Apple come during a busy period for India’s semiconductor sector. The Economic Times recently reported that Intel has entered into a partnership with Tata Electronics to explore chip manufacturing and advanced packaging at Tata’s upcoming fab and OSAT facilities in India.

Packaging plays a critical role in semiconductor production. It protects the chip, improves performance, and helps manage power and heat. These capabilities are essential for companies looking to move up the value chain in chip manufacturing.

High standards and strong government backing

Despite the potential, one source told The Economic Times that working with Apple would be challenging. Apple is known for strict quality and reliability standards, and only a small number of partners typically make it onto its approved supplier list.

CG Semi’s project has significant backing from both central and state governments. The company’s ₹7,600 crore OSAT plant is supported under the India Semiconductor Mission, a national initiative aimed at positioning India as a global hub for semiconductor and display manufacturing.

While the talks remain exploratory, a deal with Apple would be a major milestone for India’s semiconductor ambitions and a clear signal of Apple’s long-term manufacturing strategy in the country.

title.rendered: How to Clear RAM on Mac: Easy Ways to Free Up Memory

content.rendered:
Apple Macs are known for their performance and efficiency, but when a system starts feeling slow or apps take longer to open, high memory usage is often the cause. While macOS manages RAM automatically, long-running sessions, resource-intensive applications, and dozens of browser tabs can still push the system beyond its comfort zone. In such cases, clearing RAM safely can help restore the smooth performance you are accustomed to.

This post explains how to clear RAM on a Mac and monitor memory usage correctly, while avoiding common mistakes that can make things worse.

Table of Contents
  • How RAM Works on a Mac
  • Common Signs You Need to Clear RAM on a Mac
  • How to Check RAM Usage on a Mac Before Clearing It
  • Quick Ways to Clear RAM on a Mac Without Extra Tools
    • 1. Force-Quit Apps to Instantly Free RAM on a Mac
    • 2. Restart Your Mac to Completely Clear RAM
    • 3. Reduce Browser Memory Usage to Clear RAM
  • Advanced Methods to Clear RAM on a Mac for Power Users
    • 1. Use Terminal to Purge Inactive Memory on Your Mac
    • 2. Disable Heavy Login Items and Background Apps
  • Should You Use Third-Party Apps to Clear RAM on a Mac?
  • Best Practices to Avoid RAM Issues on a Mac Long Term
  • Clearing RAM on a Mac is Not Enough? It May Be Time to Upgrade
  • Summing Up…

How RAM Works on a Mac

Unlike other operating systems, macOS considers free RAM as wasted memory. This is why it fills the free memory with cached data so apps open faster and system processes run smoothly. When another app needs memory, macOS automatically reallocates it by compressing memory or moving inactive data to storage.

Because of this memory management, you don’t have to worry about low free RAM, as it’s not a problem on its own. What you actually need to look out for is memory pressure, which shows how hard your Mac is working to keep everything running.

Common Signs You Need to Clear RAM on a Mac

You may need to clear RAM if you notice:

  • Apps take longer to open or respond.
  • Frequent spinning beach balls.
  • Sudden app freezes or crashes.
  • System slowdowns during simple tasks.
  • Fans running loudly without heavy workloads.

How to Check RAM Usage on a Mac Before Clearing It

Before you restart your Mac or force quit apps to free up RAM, you must open Activity Monitor to see what’s actually using up memory. Here’s how you can:

  1. Open the Activity Monitor on your Mac.
  2. Here, click the Memory tab.
  3. Now, check out the Memory Pressure graph at the bottom:
    • Green means your Mac is handling memory well
    • Yellow means memory usage is getting high
    • Red means your Mac is struggling, and performance will suffer
  4. If memory pressure is yellow or red, clearing RAM can help immediately.

Quick Ways to Clear RAM on a Mac Without Extra Tools

If your Mac starts slowing down, these simple built-in methods let you free up RAM quickly.

1. Force-Quit Apps to Instantly Free RAM on a Mac

Now that you know whether you need to clear RAM on your Mac, you can close the apps that are consuming excessive RAM to restore smooth performance. Here’s how:

  1. In the Activity Monitor window, check out which apps are using the most memory.
  2. Double-click the process name.
  3. Click the Quit button on the pop-up window.
  4. Click the Force Quit button on the confirmation prompt.

2. Restart Your Mac to Completely Clear RAM

If your Mac’s performance feels sluggish even after clearing RAM in Activity Monitor, you can try restarting it. Restarting clears all active memory and stops background processes that have built up over time.

  1. Click the Apple icon in the top menu bar.
  2. Click Restart in the drop-down menu.

3. Reduce Browser Memory Usage to Clear RAM

Web browsers are among the biggest RAM consumers on macOS, especially when many tabs are open. Each tab runs its own process and can quietly consume significant memory. Therefore, you must:

  • Close unused tabs.
  • Remove unnecessary extensions.
  • Restart the browser occasionally.

Advanced Methods to Clear RAM on a Mac for Power Users

These advanced techniques are best suited to experienced users who want greater control over memory behaviour when standard fixes are insufficient.

1. Use Terminal to Purge Inactive Memory on Your Mac

While cached memory helps apps launch faster and improves overall responsiveness, clearing it can temporarily free up RAM in certain situations. Here’s how:

  1. Open Terminal.
  2. Enter the macOS Terminal command: sudo purge
  3. Press Return and enter your administrator password if asked.

This forces the system to rebuild caches as needed. However, remember to use this method only for troubleshooting or performance testing, such as checking how an app behaves under low-memory conditions. It is not recommended as a routine maintenance step, as macOS will naturally replenish this memory as you continue using your Mac.

2. Disable Heavy Login Items and Background Apps

Restarting your Mac won’t help if multiple apps are set to launch automatically and keep running in the background. These apps start consuming RAM the moment you sign in, reducing available memory before you even open your primary work tools.

Common examples include cloud storage clients, messaging apps, menu bar utilities, auto-updaters, and third-party system monitors. While each app may use a small amount of RAM individually, together they can create constant memory pressure throughout the day.

Here’s how you can review and disable unnecessary login items:

  1. Open the Settings app and select General in the sidebar.
  2. Here, click Login Items & Extensions on the right.
  3. Now, under the Open at Login section, remove apps you do not need running all the time.
  4. In the Allow in the Background section, turn off apps that do not require continuous background access.

Disabling these items lowers baseline RAM usage, speeds up startup time, and prevents memory from filling up immediately after a restart.

Should You Use Third-Party Apps to Clear RAM on a Mac?

Using a third-party RAM cleaner app forces macOS to clear memory that it intentionally uses for caching. This can slow your Mac down rather than speed it up.

Since macOS memory management is already optimised, manual cleaning tools won’t do much good.

Pros

  • Quick visual overview of memory usage
  • One-click app termination

Cons

  • Force macOS to clear useful cached memory
  • Can experience slow performance after cleaning
  • Often unnecessary and sometimes misleading

Best Practices to Avoid RAM Issues on a Mac Long Term

Adopting the following consistent habits can significantly reduce long-term RAM issues and keep your Mac running smoothly during daily use:

  • Use native macOS apps where possible.
  • Avoid running multiple heavy apps simultaneously.
  • Prefer optimised Apple silicon apps on newer Macs.
  • Restart your Mac every few days.
  • Close apps you are not actively using.
  • Limit browser tabs and extensions.

Clearing RAM on a Mac is Not Enough? It May Be Time to Upgrade

If the memory pressure graph stays red even after closing apps and restarting, the issue is likely hardware-related. This usually means your everyday workload exceeds the RAM available on your Mac.

In such cases, upgrading becomes the practical solution. Intel-based Macs may support RAM upgrades, depending on the model. Apple silicon Macs use unified memory, which cannot be upgraded later, making it important to choose a higher memory configuration when purchasing a new Mac.

Summing Up…

And that’s it; this is how you clear RAM on a Mac. Remember, while closing resource-intensive apps, checking memory pressure, and restarting when needed can resolve most performance slowdowns, long-term stability comes from efficient workflows and regular system maintenance.

Have these tips improved your Mac’s performance, or do you still experience RAM-related slowdowns? Share your experience or questions in the comments below.

FAQs

Is it safe to clear RAM on a Mac?

Yes. Using built-in methods like closing apps or restarting your Mac is completely safe.

How often should I clear RAM on my Mac?

Only when performance issues appear. Regular manual clearing is unnecessary.

Will clearing RAM on a Mac delete my files or apps?

No. Clearing RAM only affects temporary memory, not stored data.

Do I need a RAM cleaner app to speed up my Mac?

No. macOS handles RAM efficiently without third-party tools.

Why is my Mac using so much RAM even when nothing is open?

Background processes, cached data, and system services still use memory. This is normal unless memory pressure stays high.

Does clearing RAM on an M1 or M2 Mac work differently?

The methods are the same, but Apple silicon Macs use unified memory more efficiently, reducing the need for manual intervention.

blockGraphs.question: Is it safe to clear RAM on a Mac?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes. Using built-in methods like closing apps or restarting your Mac is completely safe.

blockGraphs.question: How often should I clear RAM on my Mac?
blockGraphs.answer: Only when performance issues appear. Regular manual clearing is unnecessary. Will clearing RAM on a Mac delete my files or apps? No. Clearing RAM only affects temporary memory, not stored data. Do I need a RAM cleaner app to speed up my Mac? No. macOS handles RAM efficiently without third-party tools. Why is my Mac using so much RAM even when nothing is open? Background processes, cached data, and system services still use memory. This is normal unless memory pressure stays high. Does clearing RAM on an M1 or M2 Mac work differently? The methods are the same, but Apple silicon Macs use unified memory more efficiently, reducing the need for manual intervention.

title.rendered: How to Set Up and Use Tap to Pay on iPhone

content.rendered:
Let’s be honest. Reaching for your card while paying bills or checking out at the grocery store feels unnecessary now. Apple’s Tap to Pay solves that by letting you make secure, contactless payments using just your iPhone. No wallet, no extra hardware, no friction.

In this guide, you will learn how Tap to Pay works, which payment methods it supports, how to set it up, and how to use it confidently for everyday payments or business transactions.

Table of Contents
  • How Tap to Pay Works on iPhone
  • Which Cards and Wallets Work with Tap to Pay on iPhone?
    • Supported Cards
    • Supported Digital Wallets
    • Supported Payment Platforms for Businesses
  • How to Set Up Tap to Pay on iPhone
    • Device Requirements
    • Step by Step Setup
  • How to Use Tap to Pay for Payments
    • Paying in Stores
    • Accepting Payments on iPhone (For Businesses)
  • Security Features of Tap to Pay
  • Benefits of Using Tap to Pay
  • Tap to Pay Not Working on iPhone? Fixes That Actually Help
  • Tap to Pay vs Other Payment Methods
  • The Future of Tap to Pay
  • Final Thoughts

How Tap to Pay Works on iPhone

Tap to Pay uses Near Field Communication (NFC) technology to securely exchange payment data when two devices are held close together.

Here is what happens behind the scenes:

  • You hold your iPhone near a payment terminal or another iPhone
  • The NFC chip establishes a secure connection
  • Your card details are replaced with a one-time encrypted token
  • Face ID, Touch ID, or passcode confirms the payment
  • The transaction completes in seconds

Your actual card number is never shared. This makes Tap to Pay extremely secure. For small businesses, it also means you can accept payments directly on an iPhone without buying POS hardware.

Which Cards and Wallets Work with Tap to Pay on iPhone?

Tap to Pay on iPhone supports a wide range of cards, wallets, and payment platforms.

Supported Cards

  • Visa
  • MasterCard
  • American Express
  • Discover (region dependent)
  • Regional debit networks such as Interac in Canada and eftpos in Australia

Most debit and credit cards with NFC support will work.

Supported Digital Wallets

  • Apple Pay
  • Debit and credit cards stored in Apple Wallet

If you are a merchant, Tap to Pay also accepts NFC-based wallets such as Google Pay, Samsung Pay, and other contactless wallets.

Supported Payment Platforms for Businesses

  • Stripe
  • Square
  • PayPal Point of Sale
  • Adyen
  • Other Apple-approved payment providers

Availability depends on country, bank, and payment provider. Always confirm support on Apple’s official documentation.

Tip

Look for the Apple Pay or contactless symbol on the terminal to confirm compatibility.

How to Set Up Tap to Pay on iPhone

Setting up Tap to Pay takes only a few minutes.

Device Requirements

  • iPhone XS or newer
  • iOS 16 or later
  • Signed in with an Apple ID
  • Face ID, Touch ID, or passcode enabled
  • Active internet connection
  • Date and Time set to Automatic

Step by Step Setup

  1. Open the Wallet app and tap the plus sign.
  2. Tap Debit or Credit Card > Continue.
  3. Now, hold the iPhone near the chip on the card or enter the card details manually.
  4. Follow the on-screen steps to verify your card with your bank.
  5. Once approved, tap and hold the card and drag it to the front of the card deck to set as default.

You can also add Apple Card or cards from supported apps using the same steps.

For businesses, install a supported payment app like Stripe or Square and enable Tap to Pay inside the app.

Note Tap to Pay supports transaction limits of up to $50,000 for digital contactless payments and $10,000 for physical contactless cards.

How to Use Tap to Pay for Payments

Once your card is added, paying is quick and consistent.

Paying in Stores

  1. Double-click the side button.
  2. Authenticate using Face ID or Touch ID.
  3. Hold the top of your iPhone near the payment reader where the Hold Here to Pay icon appears.
  4. Wait for the Done checkmark and confirmation sound.

To use a different card, tap the card stack after double pressing the side button and select another card.

Accepting Payments on iPhone (For Businesses)

  1. Open your payment app and start a new sale entry.
  2. Enter the amount to charge. You may need to select Tap to Pay as a payment method.
  3. Ask the customer to hold their contactless card or phone on your iPhone.
  4. Payment completes instantly.

Payment completes instantly. In iOS 26, Tap to Pay also works in supported apps and websites through Apple Pay checkout.

Also Read: iOS 26 Wallet App: Everything New You Need to Know

Security Features of Tap to Pay

Tap to Pay is built with multiple layers of protection:

  • End-to-end encryption
  • Tokenization (real card numbers are never shared)
  • Face ID / Touch ID authentication
  • Secure Element chip inside the iPhone
  • Apple does not store or track your transactions

Even if your iPhone is lost, payments cannot be made without biometric verification. You can also disable Apple Pay remotely using Find My.

Benefits of Using Tap to Pay

Tap to Pay stands out for a few simple reasons:

  • Fast payments that take seconds
  • No need to carry a wallet
  • Contactless and hygienic
  • Works across stores, apps, and online
  • Businesses save money on hardware

It benefits both users and merchants without changing habits.

Tap to Pay Not Working on iPhone? Fixes That Actually Help

If Tap to Pay isn’t working on your iPhone, don’t worry. Here are the most common reasons and quick fixes:

If the issue continues, the problem may be with the merchant’s terminal or payment app. Contact Apple Support or the POS provider if needed.

Tap to Pay vs Other Payment Methods

Tap to Pay vs Google Pay

  • Apple offers tighter hardware and software integration
  • Google Pay works on a wider range of Android devices
  • Both use NFC and tokenization

Tap to Pay vs Samsung Pay

  • Samsung Pay supports MST on older devices
  • Apple relies entirely on NFC
  • Apple Pay has broader app and ecosystem integration

Tap to Pay vs Contactless Cards

  • iPhone payments use biometrics
  • Cards can be lost or stolen
  • Card numbers are never exposed on iPhone

The Future of Tap to Pay

Tap to Pay continues to expand with:

  • Support for more banks and countries
  • Faster confirmations
  • Better app and subscription integration
  • Increased adoption by small and medium businesses

Mobile payments are no longer optional. They are becoming standard.

Final Thoughts

Tap to Pay on iPhone running iOS 26 is fast, secure, and genuinely practical. Whether you are buying coffee or running a small business, it removes friction from payments while keeping security front and center. Easy setup and wide support make it one of the most useful iPhone features today.

Have you started using Tap to Pay yet? Share your experience in the comments.

FAQs

Which iPhones support Tap to Pay?

iPhone XS or newer running iOS 16 or later supports Tap to Pay.

Why is Tap to Pay disabled on my iPhone?

This usually happens due to unsupported cards, outdated iOS versions, disabled NFC, or Face ID issues. Restart your iPhone, update iOS, and recheck Wallet settings.
