title.rendered: How to Use Voice Memos on iPhone in iOS 26

content.rendered:
The Voice Memos app has always been one of the handiest tools on the iPhone. In iOS 26, it’s more powerful than ever with upgraded features like smart transcription, enhanced noise reduction, improved editing tools, and Spatial Audio support.  

Whether you want to capture a quick thought, record a meeting, or save audio for a creative project, it lets you capture audio on the fly using your iPhone’s built-in mic, a Bluetooth headset, or even an external microphone. In this guide, I’ll share everything you can do in the Voice Memos app on your iPhone. So, let’s get started! 

Table of Contents
  • What's New or Improved in iOS 26
  • Getting Started: Understanding the Voice Memos Interface
  • How to Record a Voice Memo on iPhone
    • Basic Recording
    • Record in Stereo, Mono, or Spatial Audio
  • Listen to a Voice Memo and View Its Transcript
  • How to Edit Voice Memos on iPhone
    • Trim Unwanted Parts
    • Replace a Section with New Audio
    • Enhance and Clean Up Sound
    • Change Playback Speed
  • Organizing Your Voice Memos
    • Rename Recordings
    • Create & Use Folders
  • Sharing & Exporting Voice Memos
    • Export to Files and Other Apps
    • Syncing Voice Memos Across Devices
  • How to Delete a Voice Memo
  • Tips to Record High-Quality Audio on iPhone
  • Troubleshooting Common Issues
  • Record Voice Anytime, Anywhere!

What’s New or Improved in iOS 26 

iOS 26 introduces several useful enhancements, including:

  • AI-powered transcription with higher accuracy and speaker detection. 
  • Enhanced Noise Reduction to achieve cleaner recordings in noisy environments.
  • Spatial Audio recording support on newer iPhone models. 
  • Smarter auto-naming, based on location. 
  • Enhanced Sharing includes your applied settings (like layered audio) for a consistent listening experience on other devices. 
  • Improved collaboration with Notes, allowing recording Voice Memos inside a note.  
  • Audio Input Control lets you select external mics (like USB mics) for recordings. 

Getting Started: Understanding the Voice Memos Interface 

When you open Voice Memos, you’ll see a clean interface built around simplicity: 

  • Record button (big red circle) at the bottom 
  • List of your recordings displayed above 
  • A search button to quickly find old memos 
  • Pressing the back button takes you to the home page, where you can access your folders.

Tapping any recording reveals options to play, edit, enhance, or delete it. 

How to Record a Voice Memo on iPhone

Taking a voice recording is super easy. You can use your iPhone’s built-in microphone, a supported headset like AirPods, or an external microphone.

Basic Recording 

  1. Open the Voice Memos app. 
  2. Tap the red Record button. It starts instantly, showing a live waveform as you speak.
  3. Hold your iPhone mic-up (about 6-12 inches from your mouth) and speak clearly toward it. 
  4. When done, tap the red stop button.
  5. If you want to stop recording temporarily, swipe up the recorder tab and tap the Pause button. 
  6. Hit RESUME when you wish to start recording again.
  7. To review your recording, tap the Play button.
  8. Tap checkmark to finish. Your memo saves automatically with your location name.

While taking a voice memo, you can go to your home screen and use other apps as long as no other audio plays. You will see the recording progress on your Dynamic Island. Tap on it to return to the Voice Memo app.

If you are bothered by the recording start and stop tones or want to record secretly, enable Silent mode on your iPhone.

Record in Stereo, Mono, or Spatial Audio 

Depending on your iPhone model, you can choose different recording formats: 

To change recording settings: 

  1. Go to Settings > Apps > Voice Memos.
  2. Tap Recording Mode.
  3. Select from: 
    • Mono: Small file size, good for voice notes. Audio playback is the same in both ears. 
    • Stereo: Records separate left and right channels for richer sound. 
    • Spatial Audio: Creates immersive 3D audio, ideal for musicians or ambient sound capture .

On supported iPhone models, Spatial Audio is enabled by default. Voice Memos utilizes several microphones on your iPhone in this mode.

You can also change the recording quality from Settings > Apps > Voice Memos > Audio Quality. Here, choose between Lossy and Lossless.

Listen to a Voice Memo and View Its Transcript

To play a recording, simply go to Voice Memo, tap the recording you want to listen to, and hit the Play button. Use the forward and backward buttons to skip 15 seconds.

In iOS 26, voice recordings with speech now include automatic transcripts, letting you read along while listening. You can access it on iPhone 12 and later in selected languages like English, Spanish, French, German, etc.

  1. Go to Voice Memo, tap a recording, and select the waveform icon. Else, start a recording and swipe the waveform tab.
  2. Now, tap the transcript icon in the left corner to view the transcription live. Each word will be highlighted as the recording goes on.
  3. To save the recording, tap the checkmark and select Transcript.

The feature allows you to search inside transcripts to find specific words or moments. It’s especially useful for students, journalists, and content creators.

Tip

Want to share a quick bite of a voice note? Tap the recording > three-dot icon > Copy Transcript. Then paste the text anywhere you want.

How to Edit Voice Memos on iPhone

You can trim parts you don’t need, replace sections with new audio, and even enhance the recording for better clarity without leaving the app.

  1. Open Voice Memos and tap the recording you want to fix.
  2. Tap the More button (three dots ⋯) to open options.
  3. Choose Edit Recording to enter the editing interface.

Trim Unwanted Parts

Are you familiar with trimming videos using the Photos app? If yes, trimming voice memos will be familiar. It lets you cut out audio you don’t want from the beginning, middle, or end of a memo.

  1. Once in edit mode, tap the three-dot icon > Trim.
  2. You’ll see the audio waveform with yellow handles at the edges.
  3. Drag these handles inward to set the section you want to keep.
  4. Use the Play button to preview the selection.
  5. Tap Trim to keep only the chosen part and remove the rest.
  6. Tap Apply to save.

You can pinch to zoom in on the waveform for more precise control.

Replace a Section with New Audio

If you want to keep most of your recording but change one part:

  1. In Edit Recording mode, position the playhead (the vertical line) at the start of the section you want to overwrite. Pinch zoom the waveform for precision.
  2. Tap Replace and speak your new audio.
  3. Hit Stop button when finished. The new audio replaces the old part automatically.
  4. Now, tap the checkmark and select between Save as New Recording or Save Recording (changes in the existing memo).

This is perfect when you want to correct a mistake without re-recording the whole memo.

Tip

You can create a multi-layer voice memo for professional purposes, like music composition.

Enhance and Clean Up Sound

In iOS 26, Apple added easier ways to make your recordings sound clearer:

  1. Go to the editing mode, tap the control button at the bottom right corner.
  2. Toggle on Enhance Recording.

This reduces background noise and echo so your voice stands out clearer in Mono and Stereo recordings.

There is also a playback option called Skip Silence that helps you focus on the important parts when listening back.

Change Playback Speed

Voice Memos also lets you slow down or speed up playback so you can listen more efficiently or clearly.

  1. From the editing window, tap the control button.
  2. Drag the Playback Speed slider to adjust how fast or slow the audio plays.
  3. Going towards turtle means a slower speed. This is useful for lectures, complex explanations, or unclear audio.
  4. Sliding towards rabbit increases the playback speed.

The change applies instantly, so you can hear the difference right away.

Organizing Your Voice Memos

If you regularly take voice recordings, your library can become messy quickly. Here’s how to organize them:

Rename Recordings

By default, memos are named by location to group recordings made at the same place, like classrooms or offices. To rename:

  1. Tap the recording you want to rename.
  2. Select the recording name and tap the backspace on the keyboard.
  3. Enter a custom title and hit the return key to save it.

Clear names make your recordings easier to find later.

Create & Use Folders

Folders help keep your related memos in a specific group:

  1. Select a voice memo and tap the three-dot icon.
  2. Tap Move from the context menu.
  3. If you are using folders first time, it will prompt you to enter a name. Tap Save to create the folder.
  4. Now, select the folder where you want to move the memo.
  5. Next, tap the left arrow at the top left corner to see all your folders. From here, tap the plus icon to create new folders as well.

To rename or sort your folders, tap Edit on the home page. Use the hamburger icon to drag a folder up or down to reorder. Additionally, tap the three-dot icon next to the folder to Rename or Delete it.

Tip

You can mark recordings as favorites to group them in a folder. Simply, tap the three-dot icon next to a recording and select Favorite.

Sharing & Exporting Voice Memos

Voice Memos makes it easy to share your recordings with others or export them to different apps and locations.

To share a recording:

  1. Open the Voice Memos app.
  2. Tap the recording you want to share.
  3. Tap the More button (three dots ⋯) and select Share.
  4. For multiple recordings, tap Select at the top, choose the memos, and hit the Share button.

You’ll now see the standard iOS Share Sheet, where you can choose between Messages, Mail, AirDrop, WhatsApp, etc. apps to share the memo. The recipient receives the voice memo as an audio file that can be played on most devices.

Export to Files and Other Apps

When you send a recording, it exports as an .m4a file. So, the other person can’t enjoy the Spatial Audio or layered recording. To keep the audio effects intact:

  1. Tap the three-dot icon next to the recording and select Share.
  2. Now, tap Options under the file name.
  3. Select Editable and tap the checkmark.
  4. From the Share Sheet, tap Save to Files and choose a location.

This is useful if you plan to edit the audio further or keep long-term backups.

Syncing Voice Memos Across Devices

Voice Memos works seamlessly with iCloud, so your recordings stay up to date across your iPhone, iPad, and Mac. All the edits, renames, and deletions also sync in real time.

To enable syncing:

  1. Go to Settings > [your name] > iCloud.
  2. Tap See All next to Saved to iCloud.
  3. Scroll down and toggle on Voice Memos

This ensures your recordings are always backed up and accessible, even if you change devices.

How to Delete a Voice Memo

To delete a recording:

  1. Swipe left on the voice memo
  2. Tap Delete icon.

Deleted recordings move to Recently Deleted, where they can be restored within 30 days. You may recover any recording before that time period. Tap the left arrow and go to the Recently Deleted folder. Tap Select, choose the recordings, and hit Recover.

Tips to Record High-Quality Audio on iPhone

To get the best sound quality:

  • Try to record in a quiet environment.
  • Keep the microphone close to the speaker to avoid traffic, wind, and room noise.
  • Avoid covering the microphone with your hand or case.
  • Enable Studio Voice for Spatial recordings. Tap the three-dot next to a recording, select Options, and turn on Studio Voice. Adjust the slider to control the background noise levels.
  • Use an external mic with a wind muff.

This ensures clearer and more professional-sounding recordings.

Troubleshooting Common Issues

Here are quick fixes for common problems:

Record Voice Anytime, Anywhere!

Voice Memos is a powerful yet simple tool that fits seamlessly into everyday life. With features like transcription, noise reduction, and cross-device syncing, it’s no longer just a basic recorder; it’s a smart audio companion.

Whether you’re a student, professional, musician, or casual user, mastering Voice Memos can save time, boost productivity, and help you capture important moments effortlessly.

Do you use Voice Memo on your iPhone? Let me know which feature you prefer!

excerpt.rendered: Master the iPhone Voice Memos app to record and share high-quality audio for everyday and professional needs.

title.rendered: Apple Leak Reveals Foldable iPhone, AirTag 2, and Upcoming Devices

content.rendered:
A major Apple leak has revealed internal details about dozens of unreleased products, confirming Apple’s work on a foldable iPhone, AirTag 2, new Macs, iPads, wearables, and home devices.

The information was first reported by Macworld, based on data extracted from a leaked internal build of Apple’s operating system.

How the Apple Leak Happened

The leak originated from an Apple prototype device running an early internal build of iOS. The software version, 23A5234w, predates the first developer beta of iOS 26.

At the time, Apple was still referring to the operating system internally as iOS 19, which explains the older labeling inside the leaked build. Once accessed, the software revealed internal codenames tied to unreleased Apple hardware and chips.

While many of these products were already rumored, their presence inside Apple’s own software confirms they are actively being developed.

AirTag 2 and Apple Home Devices in Development

The leak confirms AirTag 2, internally known as B589, along with several upcoming Apple home and accessory products.

Confirmed devices include:

  • AirTag 2 – B589
  • HomePod mini 2 – B525
  • Apple TV (next generation) – J355
  • Home hub with base – J490
  • Mounted home hub – J491
  • Unknown home accessory – J229
  • Tabletop robot – J595
  • Apple Studio Display 2 – J427, J527

Several of these products are expected to arrive in 2026, though Apple’s internal software does not include release dates.

Foldable iPhone and Future iPhone Models

One of the most significant confirmations is Apple’s work on a foldable iPhone, listed under the codename V68. This aligns with years of reports about Apple experimenting with foldable designs.

The leak also references multiple future iPhone models:

  • iPhone 17e – V159
  • iPhone Air 2 – V62
  • iPhone 18 Pro – V63
  • iPhone 18 Pro Max – V64
  • Foldable iPhone – V68

These entries show Apple is planning several iPhone generations ahead, including experimental form factors.

Upcoming iPads and Macs Revealed

Apple’s tablet and Mac roadmap is also detailed in the leaked build.

iPads

  • iPad 12 – J581 (Wi-Fi), J582 (Cellular)
  • M4 iPad Air (11-inch) – J707 (Wi-Fi), J708 (Cellular)
  • M4 iPad Air (13-inch) – J737 (Wi-Fi), J738 (Cellular)

Macs

  • Low-cost MacBook with A18 Pro – J700
  • M5 MacBook Air – J813 (13-inch), J815 (15-inch)
  • M5 Pro/Max MacBook Pro – J714c, J714s, J716c, J716s
  • M5 Mac mini – J873g (M5), J873s (M5 Pro)
  • M5 Mac Studio – J775c (M5 Max), J775d (M5 Ultra)
  • M6 14-inch MacBook Pro – J804
  • M6 Pro/Max MacBook Pro – K114c, K114s, K116c, K116s

This confirms Apple is already preparing hardware well beyond its current M-series lineup.

Vision Headsets, Smart Glasses, and Wearables

The leak also reveals Apple’s ongoing work on spatial computing and wearables.

Referenced devices include:

  • Vision Air headset – N100
  • Cheaper Vision Pro (second generation) – N109
  • AI smart glasses – N401 (previously N50)
  • AR glasses prototype – N421 (scrapped)
  • Mac-connected AR glasses – N107 (scrapped)

Apple Watch models in development:

  • Apple Watch Series 12 – N237 (Wi-Fi), N238 (Cellular)
  • Apple Watch Ultra 4 – N240

Upcoming Apple Chips Listed Internally

The internal build also references several future Apple chips:

  • U3 Ultra Wideband – T2034
  • M5 Pro / Max / Ultra – T6050
  • M6 chip – T8152
  • A20 / A20 Pro – T8160
  • S11 – T8320

These chips align with the devices listed above and indicate Apple’s long-term silicon roadmap.

What This Leak Reveals About Apple’s Future

Apple’s internal software does not include launch timelines, but products like AirTag 2, iPads, and home devices are expected earlier, while foldable iPhones, advanced Macs, and next-generation wearables are likely planned for late 2026 and beyond.

Based entirely on information uncovered by Macworld, this leak provides one of the clearest looks yet at Apple’s long-term product pipeline.

title.rendered: Can You See Who Unfollowed You on Instagram? Here’s How

content.rendered:
No matter whether you’re a content creator or a casual Instagrammer, watching your follower count drop without any explanation can be frustrating. One moment everything looks stable, and the next, the number is lower, with no hint about who unfollowed you or when it happened. While Instagram clearly shows new followers, likes, and replies, it stays completely silent when someone unfollows you. Fortunately, there are a few indirect ways to figure it out.

This guide walks you through the most effective methods to see who unfollowed you on Instagram, without changing how you normally use the app.

Table of Contents
  • Can You See Who Unfollowed You on Instagram?
  • Method 1: Check Manually Using Instagram Search
  • Method 2: Check Recent Follows in Your Activity Section
  • Method 3: Use Instagram Data Download
  • Method 4: Use Third-Party Followers Tracking Apps
  • Why Your Follower Count Drops Without Clear Unfollows
  • Signing Off…

Can You See Who Unfollowed You on Instagram?

No, Instagram does not notify users when someone unfollows them. The only information available is your total follower count and the list of accounts currently following you. This design choice is largely about privacy. Instagram avoids putting users in uncomfortable situations where an unfollow could trigger unnecessary conflict or confrontation.

Method 1: Check Manually Using Instagram Search

If engagement from a specific account suddenly drops, such as fewer likes, comments, or Story views, it could indicate that the person has unfollowed you. While this is not always a guaranteed sign, manually checking can help confirm your suspicion.

  1. Open Instagram and head to your profile.
  2. Tap Followers to open your followers list.
  3. Here, search for the suspected Instagram account.
  4. If the account does not appear in the list, it means they are no longer following you.

This method works best when you already have a specific account in mind.

Method 2: Check Recent Follows in Your Activity Section

If you believe a recent follower has quietly unfollowed you, Instagram’s activity section can provide some clues.

  1. Open Instagram and tap the Heart button at the top right corner of your feed.
  2. Here, select the Follows tab.
  3. Here, Instagram shows a chronological list of accounts that recently followed you.
  4. Now, compare this list with your current followers list. If someone appeared in your recent follow interactions but no longer shows up in your followers list, they have likely unfollowed you.

This approach is especially useful for spotting recent unfollows, though it becomes less reliable over time.

Method 3: Use Instagram Data Download

For a broader view of who no longer follows you, Instagram’s data download feature can be surprisingly helpful.

Instagram allows you to request a copy of your account information, which includes follower and following data.

To access this, open your Instagram account’s Settings → Accounts Center → Your information and permissions → Export your information and follow the on-screen instructions.

Once the archive is ready, download and extract the files. Inside, locate the folders for followers and following. These files can then be uploaded to an AI chatbot, such as ChatGPT, where you can ask something like, “Who doesn’t follow me back on Instagram?” The AI can compare the lists and identify accounts that no longer follow you.

This method takes more effort, but it is useful if you want a clearer picture rather than checking one account at a time.

Method 4: Use Third-Party Followers Tracking Apps

There are many third-party apps that claim to show who unfollowed you on Instagram, sometimes even in real time. These apps usually work by tracking changes in your followers list over time.

That said, we at iGeekBlog do not recommend using them. Many of these apps ask for full account access or even your Instagram password, which increases the risk of hacking or data misuse. Some may also violate Instagram’s terms of service, putting your account at risk of being restricted or banned.

Why Your Follower Count Drops Without Clear Unfollows

A lower follower count does not always mean someone manually unfollowed you. Instagram regularly removes spam accounts, bots, and inactive profiles, which can cause sudden drops. Temporary account deactivations can also reduce your follower count without showing any specific unfollower. All of this happens silently, with no visible history or alerts.

Signing Off…

That’s pretty much it. While Instagram does not make unfollow tracking straightforward, it is still possible if you know where to look. The key is understanding that unfollower data is never shown directly and must be inferred through comparison and observation.

Found a method that works better for you? Let us know in the comments below.

  • How to clear Instagram cache on iPhone
  • How to see who shared your Instagram post on iPhone or desktop

title.rendered: How to Send a Text Message via Satellite on iPhone

content.rendered:
Staying connected isn’t always guaranteed, especially when you are in remote regions or facing a temporary network shutdown. That’s where satellite messaging technology steps in. Your iPhone has the option to connect to satellites orbiting Earth to send and receive messages.

With iOS 26, Apple has made satellite messaging faster, more reliable, and easier to use. In this guide, I’ll break down what satellite messaging is, how it works, which iPhones support it, and how to use it step by step, so you’re never completely off the grid.

Table of Contents
  • What Is Text Message via Satellite on iPhone and How It Works
  • Supported iPhone Models, iOS Versions, and Countries
    • Supported Countries/Regions
  • Before You Go Off-Grid
  • How to Send a Text Message via Satellite on iPhone
  • Receiving Messages via Satellite in Remote Areas
  • Using Satellite Messaging for Emergencies
    • Emergency SOS via Satellite
    • Send Location via Find My
    • Request Roadside Assistance via Satellite
  • Cost and Pricing of Satellite Messaging Services
  • Benefits of Using Satellite Messaging for iPhone Users
  • Final Thoughts: Should You Use Satellite Messaging?

What Is Text Message via Satellite on iPhone and How It Works 

Satellite messaging allows your iPhone to communicate through low-Earth-orbit satellites when cellular or Wi-Fi connections are unavailable. Instead of connecting to a tower nearby, your phone points toward a satellite in the sky to send your message. 

Here’s how it works: 

  • Your iPhone detects that you have no signal. 
  • It automatically sends a Use Messages via Satellite notification. 
  • You point your phone toward the sky so it can lock onto a satellite. 
  • Your message is compressed, optimized, and sent through the satellite network. It stays end-to-end encrypted for privacy and can take 30 seconds to a minute (or longer under trees) to send.
  • The message reaches Apple’s relay stations and then gets delivered to the recipient. 

You can send standard texts, location information, and emergency messages if needed. 

Supported iPhone Models, iOS Versions, and Countries 

Satellite texting is available on: 

  • iPhone 14 series 
  • iPhone 15 series 
  • iPhone 16 series 
  • iPhone 17 series 

These models include the necessary satellite antennas and hardware to connect to low-Earth-orbit networks. You must be running iOS 18 or later to access the latest satellite messaging features. 

However, if you purchased your iPhone in Armenia, Belarus, China mainland, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan and Russia, the feature is unavailable. In Hong Kong and Macao, satellite connectivity is only offered on iPhone 16e and later. 

Supported Countries/Regions 

Apple continues expanding availability, but satellite messaging is supported in: 

  • The United States 
  • Canada 
  • Mexico 
  • Japan 

Emergency SOS via satellite covers more countries, including parts of Europe, Australia, New Zealand, and Japan. 

Before You Go Off-Grid 

After you ensure you can access the satellite features, you need to do a basic setup while having an active internet connection: 

  • Enable iMessage: go to Settings > Apps > Message and toggle on iMessage. 
  • Active SIM: Your iPhone must have a working SIM card or eSIM. 
  • Set up Family Sharing and add emergency contact: Members of your Family Sharing group, and your emergency contacts can send you an SMS when you’re off the grid without you having to message them first. You will get their messages when you connect to a satellite.  
  • Urge your contacts to upgrade their iPhone: They must have iOS 18 or later to receive and respond to your messages via satellite.  

Tip: You may practice connecting to the satellite with the demo. Go to Settings > Apps > Messages and tap Satellite Connection Demo. 

How to Send a Text Message via Satellite on iPhone 

When you’re out of cellular range, your iPhone will automatically offer the satellite option. Here’s how to use it: 

  1. Open the Messages app and start a new conversation or open an existing one. 
    • If you have No Service, you’ll see an alert. Tap Use Messages via Satellite on the prompt.  

      Image credit: Apple
  2. Compose your message as usual. Keep it short, as satellite bandwidth is limited. 
  3. Follow the on-screen instructions to point your iPhone toward the sky. Your phone shows arrows guiding you to position it correctly. 
  4. Hold your phone steadily without raising it until the connection is established. You will see a green dot and a satellite banner on Dynamic Island. 
    • Once connected, tap the Send button. Messages may take 15–30 seconds to send, depending on the movement of the satellite. 

      Image credit: Apple

For a stronger satellite connection, stay outside with a clear view of the sky and horizon. Also, avoid tall buildings, mountains, and dense tree cover, as they may restrict the signals. Additionally, it may not work in areas above 62° latitude, such as the northern parts of Alaska.  

The best part is that your message will be sent as an SMS via satellite if the contact doesn’t use iMessage, runs an older iOS version, or has a non-Apple device. Also, if you haven’t communicated with them over iMessage in the past month or more, the message becomes SMS. 

Note You can only send and receive text messages, emojis, and Tapbacks via satellite. Sharing photos, videos, audio messages, stickers, and using group messaging are not supported.

Receiving Messages via Satellite in Remote Areas

One question people often ask is: “Can I receive messages via satellite even when I’m back in normal coverage?” 

Yes! If someone sends you a text via satellite while you have regular cellular or Wi-Fi, it will simply appear in Messages like a normal SMS. You’ll see an alert that your contact is accepting messages via satellite. To reply to the conversation: 

  1. Type your message and tap the send button. 
    • A Send via Satellite option appears under the message bubble. Tap it to successfully deliver your message. 

      Image credit: Apple

Once they have a signal, all texts sync. Thus, your friends and family can reach you without a hitch; no different than when you are using normal texting.

Using Satellite Messaging for Emergencies 

Satellite messaging is especially valuable in emergency situations. That’s why Apple added satellite SOS features to help you reach help even with no service. 

Emergency SOS via Satellite 

When you try to call emergency services with no coverage, your iPhone automatically offers Emergency SOS via Satellite. Ensure you have your Medical ID and emergency contacts set up beforehand.  

  1. On the emergency call screen, tap Emergency Text via Satellite. 
  2. Select Report Emergency. 
    • You will be prompted to answer some emergency questions (injury, stranded, trapped, etc.) to best describe your situation. 

      Image credit: Apple
  3. Now, you can alert your emergency contacts about your situation along with your location. 
  4. Follow the onscreen instructions to connect to a satellite. 
    • After you’ve connected, continue following the instructions to stay connected and deliver your message to the emergency services. 

      Image credit: Apple

Send Location via Find My 

While on a trip, I always share my location with my family and loved ones, so they can keep tabs on my whereabouts. Now, even if you go off-grid, you can continue sharing your location thanks to satellite support in Find My. 

  1. Open Find My, go to the Me tab, and select Send My Location under My Location via Satellite 
  2. Follow the onscreen instructions to connect to the satellite and send the message successfully. It may take a few minutes. 
  3. Your contacts can see your most recent location for up to 7 days, even when you’re offline. 

Great for hiking, camping, and road trips. However, you can’t see your friend’s location on Find My while on satellite.  

Request Roadside Assistance via Satellite 

In supported countries, you can request help from roadside services if your car breaks down and you have no signal.  

To get Roadside Assistance via satellite: 

  1. Open Messages and tap the pen icon. 
    • Enter Roadside in the To field. 

      Image credit: Apple
  2. Now, tap Roadside Assistance. 
    • Describe your situation like dead battery, flat tire, out of fuel, etc. along with your car model name. 

      Image credit: Apple
  3. Follow the steps to connect to a satellite and start a conversation with an assistance provider. 

Cost and Pricing of Satellite Messaging Services 

Apple has offered satellite messaging for free for the first two years on new eligible iPhones. The free period starts from your iPhone’s activation date.  

Right now, Apple has extended the trial for existing users and hasn’t made post-free-period pricing publicly fixed. 

Here’s what you need to know: 

  • Emergency SOS and all other satellite features are included at no cost as of now. 
  • Standard satellite messages can become a part of a subscription in the future.
  • Roadside assistance can come with third-party charges. 

Benefits of Using Satellite Messaging for iPhone Users 

Here’s why satellite messaging is a game changer: 

  • You can keep in touch almost everywhere, including in remote regions. 
  • Be safe during natural disasters or in case of network outages. 
  • Works seamlessly with the Messages app; no new app is needed. 
  • Location sharing improves safety for solo or adventure travelers. 
  • Privacy focused with end-to-end iMessage encryption. 
  • Emergency SOS features can truly be lifesaving. 

In short, satellite messaging brings peace of mind. It’s especially valuable for adventurers, campers, sailors, rural dwellers, or anyone in disaster-prone areas.  

Final Thoughts: Should You Use Satellite Messaging? 

Absolutely! If you value safety, travel often, or live in areas with spotty signals, satellite messaging is one of the most important features Apple has ever added. 

You may not need it every day, but the moment you find yourself without service, you’ll be glad your iPhone can still reach the outside world. iOS 26 makes the entire process smooth, intuitive, and reliable, turning your iPhone into a communication lifeline when you need it most. 

If you haven’t tried the feature yet, take the demo today and be ready for any unexpected situations. Stay safe!

keyPoints.title: Apple's Satellite Communication in iOS 18
keyPoints.explanation: iOS 18 introduces 'Messages via Satellite,' enabling iPhones to send texts directly to low Earth orbit satellites without cellular or Wi-Fi, expanding emergency and connectivity options.

keyPoints.title: Functionality of 'Messages via Satellite'
keyPoints.explanation: Supported iPhones connect to communication satellites and require users to align their device towards the satellite to successfully send messages.

keyPoints.title: Sending Messages through Satellite
keyPoints.explanation: Users need to connect to a satellite, then compose and send messages via the Messages app, with guidance provided by the Dynamic Island interface.

keyPoints.title: Monitoring Satellite Connection
keyPoints.explanation: Dynamic Island displays indicators showing satellite connection status and provides directions to re-establish connection if lost, turning green upon successful reconnection.

keyPoints.title: Current Limitations and Requirements
keyPoints.explanation: The feature is limited to certain contacts for initial messaging, may deplete battery quickly, and is available on iPhone 14 or newer models in the US and Canada.

title.rendered: 20 Best Christmas Apps for iPhone and Android to Try This Holiday Season

content.rendered:
The festive season is finally here, and our smartphones are here to make it even more special. Whether it is assistance with organizing festive events, tracking Santa, making personalized greeting cards, or even getting us into the Christmas mood, there is an app that can make all of this much easier!  

In this guide, we’ve rounded up the best Christmas apps for both iPhone and Android, so you can celebrate smarter, stay organized, and make it memorable with friends and family. 

Table of Contents
  • Christmas Cooking and Recipe Apps
    • 1. Kitchen Stories Easy Recipes
    • 2. Intent – Meal Planner
    • 3. Make Me a Cocktail
  • Christmas Gifting Apps
    • 4. Giftster: Wish List Registry
    • 5. Elfster: The Secret Santa App
    • 6. Fetch: America’s Rewards App
  • Christmas Apps for Volunteering and Finding Local Holiday Events
    • 7. Golden: Volunteer Portal
    • 8. Eventbrite
  • Christmas Game and Entertainment App
    • 9. Netflix
    • 10. Christmas Home Design Game
    • 11. Message from Santa!
    • 12. Charades – Family & Party Game
  • Christmas Collage and Memory-Making Apps
    • 13. PhotoGrid: Video Collage Maker
    • 14. PicCollage: Photo Video Editor
    • 15. MyPostcard Postcard App
  • Best Task Management Apps to Organize Your Christmas Plans
    • 16. Todoist: To Do List & Calendar
    • 17. Christmas Countdown (2025)
    • 18. TimeTree
  • Best Apps to Decorate Your Home for Christmas
    • 19. Room Planner – AI Home Design
    • 20. Wayfair – Shop All Things Home
  • Enjoy Christmas in Style!

Christmas Cooking and Recipe Apps

While mouthwatering meals are a hallmark of Christmas, the stress of planning these culinary masterpieces can be overwhelming. For those bearing the culinary torch this year, let these Christmas recipe apps transform your cooking.

1. Kitchen Stories Easy Recipes 

The Kitchen Stories provides the easiest way to find and cook delicious food, whether a beginner, a chef, a cook, or even a mother. It provides over 10,000 recipes with step-by-step guides for every diet and occasion. Recipes become more enjoyable with photos, helpful videos, and features such as adjustable serving sizes and a distraction-free cooking mode. 

You can save your favorite recipes from social media, build custom cookbooks, and get inspired every day with new ideas from a global community of food lovers. You can attend their Christmas Cookies event now. The Android app also offers the same set of features.

Download on iPhone

Price: Free (In-app purchases start from $6.99) 

2. Intent – Meal Planner

Embrace a healthier holiday season with the Intent Meal Planner. It helps you craft delicious and nutritious meals tailored to your family’s needs. Intent Healthy Plan filters your preferences for allergies and provides a measurement based on the number of guests you’ll receive this Christmas. 

That’s not all. The app also seamlessly integrates with grocery stores like Instacart, Kroger, and Walmart, allowing you to streamline your shopping from your kitchen. If you are on Android, you can try the Plan to Eat: Meal Planner app.

 Download on Android

Price: Free (In-app purchases start at $9.99)

3. Make Me a Cocktail

The Make Me a Cocktail app makes party drinks easy and fun! Just enter the ingredients you have at home, and it will show you the cocktails you can make. The app has 3500+ easy-to-follow recipes for everyone, whether you’re a beginner or an expert. You can save recipes in the Tried and Want to Try list for quick access. 

Additionally, if you are looking for cocktail ideas, you can go through different categories based on spirits, types, etc. Its intuitive interface makes cocktail mixing a fun way to impress your guests or enjoy a festive drink at home. The app is also available on the Play Store.

Download on iPhone | Download on Android

Price: Free (In-app purchases start at $0.99)

Christmas Gifting Apps

Tailoring the perfect gift for a loved one can be daunting. Leverage these gifting apps to relieve stress. For more techie gift ideas, read our detailed Apple holiday gift guide.

4. Giftster: Wish List Registry

Giftster helps you create and share wish lists for Christmas, birthdays, and more. You can add gift ideas from any store, organize them in one place, and invite family or friends to view and shop lists. Everyone receives the gifts they really want.  

The app also lets you mark items as purchased (without spoiling the surprise) to avoid duplicates, making gift planning easy and stress-free year after year. If your family member uses Android, they can also enjoy the Giftster app.

Download on iPhone | Download on Android

Price: Free

5. Elfster: The Secret Santa App

Christmas is incomplete without gift exchanges, and Elfster makes this planning a breeze. It lets you organize Secret Santa with a fun twist. Create a gift exchange, invite friends or family, and let the app handle the pairing. It works similarly on iPhone and Android. 

Worried about Christmas gift ideas? You can browse gift recommendations according to current trends in the app to make shopping easier. Additionally, if your family doesn’t have Elfster, share your wish lists with them. You can even add requests to others’ wish lists to ensure you get the ideal present.

Download on iPhone | Download on Android

Price: Free

6. Fetch: America’s Rewards App

The holiday season means lots of shopping. What if I said you can make everyday shopping more rewarding without clipping coupons or providing credit card information? Fetch is a free shopping rewards app on iPhone and Android that will make your Christmas more fun.  

Just snap a photo of your receipts from any online store, supermarket, gas station, or restaurant to earn Points, then redeem them as gift cards from popular brands like Amazon, Walmart, Target, etc. The best part is that the app notifies you about the latest deals and offers.

Download on iPhone | Download on Android

Price: Free

Christmas Apps for Volunteering and Finding Local Holiday Events

Volunteering and participating in local events offer a fulfilling way to connect with our community, spread kindness, and make a meaningful impact during the Christmas season. Locate the best ones around you with these apps. 

7. Golden: Volunteer Portal

Golden Volunteer only requires you to provide your postal address, and you’ll be on your way to finding the volunteering opportunity closest to you. You can also filter the results based on your criteria. The app provides details on volunteer opportunities across 8,000 organizations, including UNICEF and AARP. 

When you volunteer at an event, it automatically tracks your hours, engagement, and monetary donations. Additionally, you can use the Goldie AI coach to fulfill your personal goals.

Download on iPhone

Price: Free 

8. Eventbrite

Are you planning to travel to major cities this Christmas season? Find upcoming events in San Francisco, New York, Washington, and more, and create lasting memories with your loved ones right from your iPhone or Android.  

And no worries if you’re staying home for a cozy Christmas. It also recommends fun events in your area. You can follow popular organizers on Eventbrite and purchase tickets for their events. Feel free to clip an event to your calendar app to ensure you don’t miss it.

Download on iPhone | Download on Android

Price: Free 

Christmas Game and Entertainment App

Experience the joy of celebrating with others through these fun holiday games and entertainment apps for Christmas.

9. Netflix

Netflix is already popular and doesn’t need an introduction. You already know it packs plenty of festive shows, including Christmas. I know Netflix doesn’t feature real-time group streaming. You can pick an extension that adds this functionality. 

For instance, Teleparty is one such extension that adds group watching to Netflix. Don’t hesitate to gather your loved ones for a cinematic escape on Netflix.

Download on iPhone | Download on Android

Price: Free (In-app purchases start at $17.99)

10. Christmas Home Design Game

A list of the best Christmas apps is incomplete without a fun game. So, let me introduce you to Christmas Home Design. It is a classic matching video game that packs all the holiday fun you will need. Decorate rooms with festive ornaments, wreaths, candles, and light up the trees. 

You can also find festive items by solving match-3 puzzles, and much more. No lives to lose or races to win; you can relax and enjoy the game for as long as you want on your iPhone and Android.

Download on iPhone | Download on Android

Price: Free (In-app purchases start at $0.99)

11. Message from Santa!

If you have kids at home, this is a must-have app. The Message from Santa app brings Santa’s magic right to your iPhone. It offers personalized calls, texts, and even video messages from Santa himself. 

You can also call Santa’s voicemail to record your wish list and track what Santa is doing right now. It’s a fun way to keep the Christmas spirit alive and make your little ones feel extra special this holiday season!

Download on iPhone

Price: Free (In-app purchases start at $1.49)

12. Charades – Family & Party Game

 

Charades game is a fun and easy way to bring people together for laughs, challenges, and unforgettable moments. The app gives you 87+ themed decks to choose from. Just hold your phone up, let others act or describe the word, and try to guess it before time runs out. The gameplay is fast-paced and energetic, suitable for all players. It’s also available on Android.

Download on iPhone | Download on Android

Price: Free (In-app purchases start from $0.99) 

Christmas Collage and Memory-Making Apps

What’s more fun than creating memories with collages this Christmas? Here are some iPhone apps for that.

13. PhotoGrid: Video Collage Maker

PhotoGrid features every tool to help you relive your Christmas experience. You can quickly combine your photos and videos with creative layouts and festive AI filters. Advanced AI editing tools help you generate realistic holiday images.  

The iOS and Android app also offer Christmas AI video effects and 20,000+ templates to keep the holiday spirit going. You can add stickers, text, and filters and share your collages with loved ones. Moreover, you can use it to create Christmas cards.

Download on iPhone | Download on Android

Price: Free (In-app purchases start at $0.99) 

14. PicCollage: Photo Video Editor

PicCollage has always been a lifesaver for creating Christmas greeting collages, and I’ll recommend it repeatedly. Featuring a range of frame overlays and holiday backgrounds, it helps transform your Christmas memories into stunning collages. 

You can choose from existing templates or create one from scratch. For a touch of personalization, feel free to add stickers to your greeting collages and share them with loved ones. If you are on Android, download it from the Play Store.

Download on iPhone | Download on Android

Price: Free (In-app purchases start at $0.99)

15. MyPostcard Postcard App

Handwritten greetings feel special when crafted with love. That’s what this postcard app helps you achieve. You can send stunning seasonal postcards directly from your iPhone or Android device with ease. The app lets you personalize them with photos, heartfelt messages, and your signature. 

There’s also an option to create a customized photo calendar. Overall, it’s another nifty way to bring smiles to the faces of your loved ones this Christmas.

Download on iPhone | Download on Android

Price: Free (In-app purchases start from $0.99) 

Best Task Management Apps to Organize Your Christmas Plans

If you’re likely to forget to turn on the Christmas lights or prepare some cookies and a glass of milk for Santa, these dependable task apps will help you keep track of your Christmas routines. 

16. Todoist: To Do List & Calendar

ToDoist has never failed me as a trusty sidekick during Christmas. It’s a personal task management app that helps you schedule tasks, set reminders, and prioritize them by importance. 

Want to assign some tasks to someone else, so they get done quicker? Feel free to share your to-do list with that close pal, whether they are on iPhone or Android. Task sharing ensures everyone is on the same page, preventing holiday chaos.

Download on iPhone | Download on Android

Price: Free (In-app purchases start at $6.99) 

17. Christmas Countdown (2025)

When a festival is just around the corner, it is fun to mark down the remaining days. A countdown app can help you track the exact days, hours, minutes, and even seconds left until Christmas. 

We love this one because you can choose from different characters, including Santa, a snowman, a Christmas tree, a reindeer, and a skater. Moreover, you can track heartbeats & sleep remaining until 25th December, and easily share them on social media from your iPhone and Android devices.

Download on iPhone | Download on Android

Price: Free (In-app purchases start at $1.99)

18. TimeTree

TimeTree is a shared calendar app designed to make organizing schedules with others easy and stress-free. You can create calendars for family and friends, and everyone can add or view events in one place. It helps you stay on the same page by keeping plans, reminders, and notes organized and accessible across devices, including iPhone and Android.

With its clean design and real-time updates, it’s a convenient way to avoid miscommunication and ensure everyone stays connected.

Download on iPhone | Download on Android

Price: Free (In-app purchases start from $1.99)

Best Apps to Decorate Your Home for Christmas

Your aesthetics define your ambiance, and you need your atmosphere to be as stunning as possible this Christmas. These apps are a sure way to embrace your inner designer and transform your home into a Christmas wonderland. 

19. Room Planner – AI Home Design

From traditional to modern designs, Room Planner lets you create the perfect Christmas look for your home. Start with blank rooms or draw inspiration from pre-designed options. Feel free to browse ideas, refine room details, and choose from styles such as transitional, mid-century modern, and Memphis. 

You can also take cues for your Christmas designs from a global community of room designers and seamlessly edit their creations to match your unique style. Share your holiday-inspired decoration designs with friends and family to spread the festive cheer. It’s also available on iPhone and Android.

Download on iPhone | Download on Android

Price: Free (In-app purchases start at $5.99) 

20. Wayfair – Shop All Things Home

With Wayfair’s augmented-reality feature, you’re the creative maestro, effortlessly transforming your home into the Christmas haven you envision. Imagine your living room in the warm glow of a twinkling Christmas tree, your dining table with festive centerpieces, and every corner of your home radiating the warmth of Christmas. 

Featuring an endless selection of furniture, rugs, decor, and kitchenware, Wayfair lets you design your home just as planned. It also includes clues to help you discover the perfect pieces that match your style and budget. As a bonus, you also receive free shipping on eligible orders.

Download on iPhone

Price: Free 

Enjoy Christmas in Style! 

As the enchanting spirit of Christmas fills the air, I hope these apps bring a touch of magic and joy to your Christmas celebration. If you have any favorite Christmas apps that I missed, please share them in the comments below. I’d love to hear about the apps that make your holiday season extra special. 

¡Feliz Navidad!

title.rendered: Apple’s Upcoming iOS Updates: Insights from Internal Leaks

content.rendered:
A recent internal iOS 26 build leak has unveiled plans for Apple’s future software updates, detailing what could be in store for iOS 26.4, iOS 27, and even iOS 28. This information, shared by MacWorld, provides a rare glimpse into Apple’s development processes.

Apple engineers test upcoming features years in advance using special development “flags,” which help them toggle functionality and make notes about feature specs and anticipated release timelines.

Health App Gets Major Redesign

Major updates are on the horizon for Apple’s Health app. According to the leak, users can expect a revamped category layout that enhances navigation and streamlines health data recording.

A new addition called Health+ is also in the works. This would be a subscription service using AI to offer personalized health advice, acting much like a virtual health consultant.

Siri Overhaul Still on Track for iOS 26.4

Despite some initial engineering challenges noted last October, Apple’s digital assistant, Siri, is primed for major enhancements in iOS 26.4. The aim is to support more natural and context-aware conversations.

These changes might be powered by a collaboration with Google, which involves integrating Google’s Gemini technology, a sign of Apple’s commitment to modernizing Siri.

AirPods Pro 3 to Get Precise Location Tracking

For AirPods Pro 3 owners, “Precise Outdoor Location” functionality is on the way in iOS 26.4. This feature promises more accurate positioning within the Find My app, but it seems to be limited to models featuring the new U2 chip.

Credit Card Autofill Expands Beyond Safari

Apple is experimenting with a broader application of credit card autofill that would span beyond just Safari, extending to third-party apps. Users could save and autofill payment details securely across all apps via iCloud Keychain.

When entering card details in a third-party app, a prompt would appear, offering to save this information to iCloud Keychain, making future transactions more seamless.

Freeform App Adds Folder Organization

Folder support is on the horizon for the Freeform collaborative app, according to the iOS 26.4 leak. This should make organizing projects much simpler, with the added benefit of iCloud synchronization to keep content consistent across all devices.

Apple TV App May Introduce Sports Bundle

Hints of a “Sports Tier” within the Apple TV app suggest new sports-centric offerings might arrive by spring 2026. While specifics remain cloudy, possibilities include reorganizing current sports subscriptions or possibly a new sports streaming bundle.

With Apple reportedly gearing up to offer Formula 1 streaming, they might aim to consolidate sports content into a single subscription.

Enhanced Security for Apple ID Login

The leak points to iOS 26.4 implementing device integrity checks prior to granting Apple ID or iCloud access. This step would block jailbroken or altered devices from connecting to Apple’s cloud services.

iOS 27 and iOS 28 Features in Development

Looking even further ahead, the leak includes flags for iOS 27, showcasing potential features like improved photo collections and a new system for AirPods pairing that will work faster through backend upgrades.

For iOS 28, increased Apple Watch sleep tracking metrics are in the pipeline, potentially including “time spent in bed” measurements. There’s also talk of bringing the Health app to macOS 28, integrating health tracking with Macs.

Other Hardware Updates in the Leak

Additional revelations from the internal build feature plans for future hardware. These include a Studio Display 2 sporting 120Hz ProMotion, second-gen AirTags with enhanced tracking and battery features, and the eagerly awaited Apple smart home hub.

From iPhones and MacBooks to Android phones and AI tools, I’ve always enjoyed turning complicated features into simple, jargon-free guides. Recently, I switched sides and joined the Apple camp. Whether you want to try out new features, catch up on the latest news, or tweak your Apple devices, I’m here to help you get the most out of your tech.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio: With over 5 years of hands-on tech writing experience and more than 900 published articles, I’ve explored the best of Apple, Android, and Chrome OS. From iPhones and MacBooks to Pixel devices and Chromebooks, I break down complex features into simple, relatable guides—minus the jargon. Whether you’re customizing your iPhone, troubleshooting your Android, or tweaking Chrome OS settings, my goal is to help you get more out of your tech.

title.rendered: iOS 26.2: New Features and Security Updates

content.rendered:
Apple has officially released iOS 26.2, a mid-cycle update that focuses on useful everyday improvements, design tweaks, and important security fixes. While it is not a major redesign, the update adds several practical features across Reminders, Lock Screen, AirDrop, Apple Music, and system safety.

Table of Contents
  • Reminders Can Now Act Like Alarms
  • Lock Screen Gets Deeper Liquid Glass Controls
  • Liquid Glass Accessibility Conflicts Are Now Clearer
  • AirDrop Adds Extra Protection for Unknown Users
  • Apple Music Adds Offline Lyrics
  • Sleep Score Ranges Have Been Reworked
  • Podcasts App Gains Smart Navigation Tools
  • Passwords App Adds Better Control
  • Freeform Adds Tables for Better Organization
  • Apple News Gets a Cleaner Layout
  • Home App Supports Multipack Accessories
  • Flash for Alerts Can Use the Screen
  • Enhanced Safety Alerts Arrive in the US
  • Measure App Gets a Visual Refresh
  • Games App Adds Better Sorting and Controller Support
  • CarPlay Lets You Hide Pinned Messages
  • Faster Menu Animations
  • Privacy Disclosure Update
  • AirPods Live Translation Expands to the EU
  • Major Changes for iPhone Users in Japan
  • App Store Changes Coming to Texas
  • iPadOS 26.2 Improves Multitasking
  • Bug Fixes and Security Updates
  • Compatibility and What’s Next

Reminders Can Now Act Like Alarms

iOS 26.2 adds alarm-style alerts to the Reminders app. You can enable this by turning on the Urgent toggle while creating a reminder.

When the reminder triggers, it behaves like a real alarm with snooze and stop options. If you snooze it, a Live Activity countdown appears on the Lock Screen, letting you complete or reschedule the reminder quickly. Apple visually separates these alerts using a blue alarm color so they do not get confused with normal alarms.

Lock Screen Gets Deeper Liquid Glass Controls

The Lock Screen clock now includes a Liquid Glass slider. You can fine-tune how transparent or frosted the time appears instead of choosing a fixed look.

If you prefer clarity, there is still a Solid toggle to disable the glass effect completely. Color options for the clock remain unchanged.

Liquid Glass Accessibility Conflicts Are Now Clearer

When using the Tinted Liquid Glass option, iOS 26.2 now clearly warns that it cannot be used with Reduce Transparency or Increase Contrast accessibility settings.

Turning on Tinted mode can automatically disable those accessibility options, avoiding the manual steps required in earlier versions.

AirDrop Adds Extra Protection for Unknown Users

AirDrop is more secure in iOS 26.2. When sharing files with unknown contacts, you can now generate a temporary AirDrop code on the receiving device.

The sender must enter this code to complete the transfer. These codes remain valid for 30 days and can be managed in Settings > General > AirDrop > Manage Known AirDrop Contacts.

Apple Music Adds Offline Lyrics

Apple Music now lets you view song lyrics even when you are offline. This works for downloaded tracks and is useful when traveling or saving mobile data.

The Favorite Songs playlist has also been promoted to the Top Picks section on the Home tab.

Sleep Score Ranges Have Been Reworked

Apple has adjusted Sleep Score ranges in iOS 26.2 and watchOS 26.2 so scores better match how rested users feel.

The scoring system still totals 100 points, split across sleep duration, bedtime consistency, and interruptions. The top tier is now called Very High instead of Excellent. Sleep Scores appear in the Health app and work on all Apple Watches that support watchOS 26.2.

Podcasts App Gains Smart Navigation Tools

The Podcasts app now supports automatically generated chapters. You can also see mentions of other podcasts and tap links referenced during an episode directly from the episode page.

Passwords App Adds Better Control

In the Passwords section of Settings, you can now manage websites where passwords should not be saved. This gives more control over sign-in behavior on specific sites.

Freeform Adds Tables for Better Organization

Freeform now supports tables that can contain text, images, files, and drawings. Cells resize automatically, making it easier to organize complex boards.

Apple News Gets a Cleaner Layout

Apple News now shows quick-access category buttons for sections like Sports, Business, Food, and Puzzles. There is also a separate Following tab that is no longer tied to search.

Home App Supports Multipack Accessories

If you buy smart home accessories in a bundle, iOS 26.2 lets you pair multiple devices using a single setup code in the Home app.

Flash for Alerts Can Use the Screen

The Flash for Alerts accessibility feature now supports screen flashing for notifications. You can choose screen flash, LED flash, or both at the same time.

Enhanced Safety Alerts Arrive in the US

A new Enhanced Safety Alerts section lets users manage earthquake and imminent threat alerts. These alerts include maps and safety links and use location data for better accuracy. This feature is limited to the United States.

Measure App Gets a Visual Refresh

The Measure app’s level tool now uses a Liquid Glass design with transparent bubbles instead of solid white indicators.

Games App Adds Better Sorting and Controller Support

You can now sort your game library by size. iOS 26.2 also adds real-time challenge score updates, controller navigation, and improved support for Backbone and Razer controllers.

CarPlay Lets You Hide Pinned Messages

Drivers can now disable pinned messages in CarPlay to return to the older Messages layout.

Faster Menu Animations

Pop-out menus now use a quicker, bouncier animation similar to what Apple previewed at WWDC.

Privacy Disclosure Update

After installing iOS 26.2, Apple shows a new privacy notice explaining how Apple Account data is collected and used.

AirPods Live Translation Expands to the EU

AirPods Live Translation is now available in the European Union after delays related to the Digital Markets Act. It works with AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, and AirPods 4 with ANC, supporting multiple major languages.

Major Changes for iPhone Users in Japan

iOS 26.2 introduces several Japan-specific updates. Users can choose a different default voice assistant for the Side Button, select a preferred search engine during setup, and install third-party app stores. These changes align with regional regulations.

App Store Changes Coming to Texas

To comply with Texas law starting in 2026, Apple is adding age verification and parental consent systems. Developers will receive age range data and must support parental controls for app access.

iPadOS 26.2 Improves Multitasking

On iPad, iOS 26.2 restores drag-and-drop multitasking from the App Library, Dock, and Spotlight into Slide Over and tiled views.

Bug Fixes and Security Updates

Apple fixed over 20 security vulnerabilities, including two actively exploited WebKit bugs. Other fixes address Apple Music release issues, privacy mislabeling, FaceTime remote control bugs, and hidden photo access problems.

Apple strongly recommends updating due to the public disclosure of these vulnerabilities.

Compatibility and What’s Next

iOS 26.2 is available for all iPhones that support iOS 26. Apple is expected to release the first iOS 26.3 beta soon.

title.rendered: Dockcase Selfix Case Introduces Rear AMOLED Display for iPhone 17 Pro Selfies

content.rendered:
Dockcase has announced its latest accessory, the Selfix case, designed exclusively for the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max. Addressing a common issue for iPhone users, this case includes a small rear display that lets you use the phone’s main camera for selfies and group photos.

A Rear Display That Works Like a Live Viewfinder

The standout feature of the Selfix case is a 1.6 inch circular AMOLED display placed on the back of the phone. It offers a 480 × 480 resolution and supports touch input. The screen mirrors the rear camera view and works as a live viewfinder, allowing you to see proper framing before taking a photo.

This makes solo selfies and group shots easier, without guessing or flipping the phone around. Dockcase says the display feels natural to use and does not affect how the phone feels in hand.

Using the iPhone’s Main Camera for Selfies

The rear camera on the iPhone 17 Pro is far more capable than the front camera. With the Selfix case, users can take selfies using the 48MP main camera. This results in sharper details, better color accuracy, and wider framing.

This is especially useful for group photos or situations where image quality matters more than convenience.

Built In Charging and Storage Expansion

Along with the rear display, the Selfix case adds several practical features:

  • 100W PD 3.0 USB C port for fast charging
  • microSD card slot with support for up to 2TB of storage
  • Dedicated power button to turn off the rear display when not in use

The case works instantly after attachment. No app installation is required, and Dockcase claims the rear display has no noticeable lag.

Launch Plans and Availability

Dockcase plans to launch the Selfix case through a Zackstarter campaign. Early details suggest three color options: Blush Pink, Oat White, and Midnight Black. Pricing has not been announced yet.

If the final product performs as promised, the Selfix case could be a practical upgrade for iPhone 17 Pro users who want better selfies without extra accessories.

excerpt.rendered: A new Dockcase case gives the iPhone 17 Pro a rear AMOLED screen, letting users take high-quality selfies with the main camera.

title.rendered: Instagram Now Lets You Fine Tune Your Reels Recommendations

content.rendered:
Tired of random Reels appearing in your Instagram feed even after resetting the algorithm? Instagram has something new for you. The social media platform has introduced a powerful new tool called Your Algorithm that lets you see why certain Reels appear in your feed and gives you direct control over the recommendations you receive. Instead of feeling dictated by the algorithm, you can now fine-tune the topics you enjoy and reduce the content you prefer to avoid.

Keep reading to learn everything you need to know about Instagram’s new Your Algorithm tool.

Table of Contents
  • What Is the Instagram New Your Algorithm Tool and Why It Matters?
  • How the Instagram Algorithm Worked Before Your Algorithm Tool
  • How to Access the Instagram Reels "Your Algorithm" Panel
  • Everything You Can Do in Your Algorithm Panel on Instagram
    • 1. Review the Topics Influencing Your Reels Feed
    • 2. Customize the Reels Algorithm to Your Liking
    • 3. Share Your Reels Algorithm in Your Story
  • Using Instagram's New Your Algorithm Tool to Improve Your Experience
  • Your Reels, Your Rules…

What Is the Instagram New Your Algorithm Tool and Why It Matters?

Your Algorithm is Instagram’s latest AI-powered feature that reveals the topics that Instagram thinks you are interested in based on your recent activity on the platform. It displays how your previous interactions have shaped your Reels feed and even lets you adjust or reset those topic preferences. This way, you can have greater control over your Reels feed and keep it personalized.

If you have ever felt that the Reels tab is out of sync with your preferences, this tool is the simplest way to correct it.

How the Instagram Algorithm Worked Before Your Algorithm Tool

Before this update, Instagram followed your in-app behaviour and quietly updated your preferences in the background. The app interpreted watch time, likes, shares, and other interactions to build an interest profile.

However, you could not see or manage these inferred topics directly. This meant that if your feed drifted away from the actual interests, you had to rely on indirect methods, such as resetting the algorithm or manually interacting with new content. Your Algorithm solves this by allowing you to see and edit the underlying interest signals.

How to Access the Instagram Reels “Your Algorithm” Panel

The feature is currently limited to the U.S. as it’s still in the early phase and will roll out globally soon. If you’re in the U.S., here’s how you can access Instagram’s new Your Algorithm tool:

  1. Open the Instagram app and head to the Reels tab.
  2. Here, look for the icon with two lines and hearts in the top-right corner.
  3. Tap the icon to open Your Algorithm panel.

Everything You Can Do in Your Algorithm Panel on Instagram

Now that you know how you can access the Your Algorithm panel, here’s everything you can do in it:

1. Review the Topics Influencing Your Reels Feed

When you first open the Your Algorithm panel, you see a summary of topics generated from your activity. These topics reflect the kind of Reels you watch, like, share, save, replay, or skip.

Each topic displayed here directly influences the type of content that appears on your Reels tab, and reviewing it helps you understand exactly which interests are driving your feed. If something feels outdated or irrelevant, you can update it immediately.

2. Customize the Reels Algorithm to Your Liking

This is the true value of the feature. You can add topics you want more of or remove topics you no longer enjoy, and Instagram will update your Reels recommendations in real time. You can therefore maintain a clean, personalized feed without relying solely on passive interactions like likes or watch time.

3. Share Your Reels Algorithm in Your Story

You can also share your personalized topic summary in your Story by tapping the Share button. This is a creative way to show your followers the interests that shape your Reels recommendations.

Using Instagram’s New Your Algorithm Tool to Improve Your Experience

Your Algorithm gives you a direct way to refine your feed. If you want more travel content, you can add travel-related topics. If you want fewer unrelated Reels, you can quickly remove the related topics from your summary.

The tool helps you quickly correct your feed without waiting for the algorithm to catch up to your preferences. It is also helpful for people who feel their Reels feed becomes repetitive or irrelevant over time.

Your Reels, Your Rules…

Instagram’s Your Algorithm tool gives you more influence over what you see. With clear topic summaries and an easy way to modify them, you can now reshape your Reels feed in minutes. Once the feature rolls out globally, it will become one of the most useful controls for anyone who wants a personalized Instagram experience.

Have you tried the new Your Algorithm tool yet? Share your experience in the comments.

Related articles worth reading:

  • How to Auto Scroll on Instagram Reels

title.rendered: Best Headphone Jack Adapters for iPhone (2026)

content.rendered:
Apple ditched the trusty 3.5mm headphone jack to make their iPhone sleeker. But let’s not forget that not all of us are ready to abandon our wired headphones, studio gear, and AUX connections for cars. That where a headphone jack adapter plays a lifesaving role.

These little dongles let you connect your iPhone to headphones, mixers, speakers, and audio interfaces with a 3.5 mm plug. In this guide, you will learn how to choose the right Lightning or USB-C to 3.5 mm headphone adapter and discover the best options available for your iPhone.

Table of Contents
  • How to Choose a Good iPhone Headphone Jack Adapter
  • 6 Best 3.5mm Headphone Jack Adapters for iPhone
    • 1. Apple USB-C to 3.5 mm Headphone Jack Adapter
    • 2. UGREEN 3.5mm Headphone Adapter
    • 3. Anker USB-C to 3.5 mm Adapter
    • 4. Subynanal 2-in-1 Lightning Headphone Adapter
    • 5. JSAUX 3.5mm Headphone Jack Adapter
    • 6. Stouchi 2-in-1 Audio Adapter
  • Which Adapter Is Best for You?
  • Common Mistakes to Avoid
  • Final Verdict

How to Choose a Good iPhone Headphone Jack Adapter 

There are lots of adapters available in the market. However, some sound terrible, while others break in weeks or simply stop working. So, before buying any adapter, keep these factors in mind: 

  • Connector Type: Newer iPhones (iPhone 15+) use USB-C, while older models use Lightning. Choose the adapter that matches your phone’s port. 
  • Built-In DAC: A DAC (digital-to-analog converter) supporting 24-bit/96kHz or higher ensures clear sound, better bass, and less distortion. 
  • Check Mic & Remote Support: If you take calls or use wired earbuds with inline control, check that your adapter also supports them.    
  • Durability: Adapters are yanked, twisted, and stashed in pockets. So, look for reinforced connectors, flexible strain relief, or aluminum housings.
  • Charging: Not all headset audio splitters support fast charging and audio simultaneously. Often, cheap reproductions fall flat.

With this in mind, it becomes easy to avoid cheap imitations that concentrate on costs rather than performance.

6 Best 3.5mm Headphone Jack Adapters for iPhone

Here are some of the best adapters available for reliability, sound quality, and compatibility.

1. Apple USB-C to 3.5 mm Headphone Jack Adapter 

The official Apple adapter is the gold standard for iPhone 15 and later. At $9, I’d say it’s a no-brainer if you want a compact, sleek, and reliable adapter. With a good DAC, you can experience clean and well-balanced audio even when you’re playing back audio at max volume.

Best for: Users who want guaranteed compatibility and reliable sound. 

2. UGREEN 3.5mm Headphone Adapter

UGREEN adapter is popular because it blends solid DAC performance, Hi-Fi sound, mic and inline control support, and strong durability. The cable has braided nylon covering, aluminum alloy housings, and strain relief for longevity.  

If you have an older iPhone, you can get UGREEN Lightning to 3.5 mm Adapter. It has the same durable build, good audio quality, and MFi Certification.

Moreover, UGREEN offers a 2-in-1 Headphone Adapter and Charger combo. In addition to the fantastic audio features, you get 60W fast charging support. It’s useful if you frequently switch between charging and audio adapters. 

Best for: Strong build quality and clean sound at a budget price. 

3. Anker USB-C to 3.5 mm Adapter 

Anker’s adapter is known for clean, distortion-free audio and heavy-duty durability. Many buyers choose this specifically because Anker cables last longer than most. The tough braided nylon exterior and durable connector can withstand 15,000 bends.

This 4-inch cable can connect to your headphones, earbuds, or any other 3.5 mm AUX device and support mic and in-line controls. Anker offers an 18-month warranty to keep you worry-free.

Ideal for: People who want durability first. 

4. Subynanal 2-in-1 Lightning Headphone Adapter

If you’re always on the go or regularly have long calls, this 2-in-1 USB-C to 3.5mm adapter lets you charge while using wired headphones. You can get up to 60W PD fast charging and mic and inline controls support.

It’s compact and only 13 cm long, making it portable. Also, the high-quality DAC ensures crisp sound. The nickel-plated connectors, aluminum shell, and Kevlar braided wires make the adapter long-lasting.

Best for: Charging and listening simultaneously in a durable build. 

5. JSAUX 3.5mm Headphone Jack Adapter 

JSAUX offers rugged, braided-nylon, premium aluminum covering adapter that is surprisingly affordable. As per the brand, the tangle-free stress-relief design cable is tested for 15,000 bends. This also has full MFi certification, making it stable across iOS versions. 

You can control volume, skip music, answer the calls, use Siri as usual, and work on your iPhone with the adapter. If you use an older iPhone, go for the JSAUX Lightning to 3.5 mm Adapter. 

Best for: Rugged and reliable option.

6. Stouchi 2-in-1 Audio Adapter

Stouchi’s 2-in-1 adapter is one of the more reliable splitters for people who must charge and listen at the same time. It supports up to 30W fast charging without audio dropouts. You can enjoy Hi-Fi audio through the adapter thanks to the Hi-Res DAC chip.

The cable is made from a high-tensile braided nylon exterior and an aluminum alloy casing that is oxidation-resistant and anti-scratch. However, it’s slightly bulkier than Apple’s adapter.

Best for: Fast-charging and lossless audio simultaneously. 

Which Adapter Is Best for You? 

Here’s a quick overview so you can make a wise decision:

Common Mistakes to Avoid 

  • Buying non-certified Lightning adapters: These often stop working after iOS updates. 
  • Choosing the wrong connector: Always match your iPhone model. 
  • Cheap adapters for high-end audiophile headphones: Some adapters struggle with high-impedance gear. 
  • Ignoring mic/control compatibility: Not all adapters support calls or inline buttons. 
  • Buying ultra-cheap adapters: They can break in weeks. 

Also, when plugging/unplugging, don’t press on the connectors. Avoid tightly bending the cable.

Final Verdict 

Wired headphones aren’t going anywhere, and if you want the best experience with your iPhone, a good headphone jack adapter makes all the difference.

Apple’s official adapter is the safest pick, but brands like UGREEN, Anker, and JSAUX offer better durability and equally strong audio quality. If you need audio + charging, Stouchi or Subynanal are the most reliable options. 

In the end, it boils down to your needs and usage habits. A good quality adapter results in a better experience with improved audio, fewer bugs, and a hassle-free experience. Which 3.5mm adapter do you add to your cart. Let me know in the comments below!

@graph.name: Apple USB-C to 3.5 mm Headphone Jack Adapter
@graph.description: The official Apple adapter is the gold standard for iPhone 15 and later. At $9, I’d say it’s a no-brainer if you want a compact, sleek, and reliable adapter. With a good DAC, you can experience clean and well-balanced audio even when you’re playing back audio at max volume.

@graph.name: UGREEN 3.5mm Headphone Adapter
@graph.description: UGREEN adapter is popular because it blends solid DAC performance, Hi-Fi sound, mic and inline control support, and strong durability. The cable has braided nylon covering, aluminum alloy housings, and strain relief for longevity.

@graph.name: Anker USB-C to 3.5 mm Adapter
@graph.description: Anker’s adapter is known for clean, distortion-free audio and heavy-duty durability. The tough braided nylon exterior and durable connector can withstand 15,000 bends. This 4-inch cable can connect to your headphones, earbuds, or any other 3.5 mm AUX device and support mic and in-line controls.

@graph.name: Subynanal 2-in-1 Lightning Headphone Adapter
@graph.description: If you’re always on the go or regularly have long calls, this 2-in-1 USB-C to 3.5mm adapter lets you charge while using wired headphones. You can get up to 60W PD fast charging and mic and inline controls support.

@graph.name: JSAUX 3.5mm Headphone Jack Adapter
@graph.description: JSAUX offers rugged, braided-nylon, premium aluminum covering adapter that is surprisingly affordable. As per the brand, the tangle-free stress-relief design cable is tested for 15,000 bends. This also has full MFi certification, making it stable across iOS versions.

@graph.name: Stouchi 2-in-1 Audio Adapter
@graph.description: Stouchi’s 2-in-1 adapter is one of the more reliable splitters for people who must charge and listen at the same time. It supports up to 30W fast charging without audio dropouts. You can enjoy Hi-Fi audio through the adapter thanks to the Hi-Res DAC chip.

title.rendered: AirTag 2 Leak Unveils Five Key Upgrades Before Launch

content.rendered:
A refreshed AirTag expected in 2025 seemed likely to miss its mark as the year closes out. Yet, recent leaks indicate Apple’s next-gen tracker might be closer to release than previously thought, boasting several notable advancements.

Five Upgrades Spotted in iOS 26 Code

In a revealing report, Filipe Espósito from Macworld identified references to AirTag 2 within a leaked build of iOS 26. Espósito, who recently shared insights on updates for the next Studio Display, points to some leaked code strings for these findings.

Espósito’s analysis found that AirTag 2, now internally tagged as “2025AirTag,” could feature several enhancements:

  • A streamlined pairing process
  • Boosted Precision Finding capabilities
  • More detailed battery level tracking
  • “Improved Moving,” potentially enhancing in-motion tracking
  • Enhanced accuracy in crowded settings

Based on these code indications, Apple seemed to have aimed for a 2025 release for the updated AirTag. Whether they can still deliver within this timeframe is uncertain.

New HomePod Mini Also Referenced

The same leaked iOS code points to the development of a new HomePod mini featuring an S10 chip. Earlier leaks have suggested a refresh, and this latest discovery backs up the notion that Apple is working on an updated model.

Are You Planning to Upgrade?

Do these rumored advancements make AirTag 2 an appealing upgrade for you? We’d love to hear your thoughts in the comments.

excerpt.rendered: New iOS 26 leaks reveal Apple’s next AirTag with smoother pairing, better Precision Finding and smarter tracking. The code also hints at a refreshed HomePod mini coming soon.
